It found that among firms using AI, almost 80% said they can handle more work without increasing resources, while over 70% said it cut costs by absorbing administrative work once done by support staff.
paras.zh: 这是根据法律软件公司 Clio 发布的《2026 年英国和爱尔兰法律洞察报告》得出的结论。报告发现，在使用人工智能的公司中，近 80% 的公司表示，他们可以在不增加资源的情况下处理更多工作，而超过 70% 的公司表示，人工智能可以通过吸收曾经由支持人员完成的行政工作来削减成本。

paras.en: As a result, AI is challenging some of the assumptions on which the legal profession was built, forcing firms to reevaluate how their lawyers spend their time, how they charge for it and how new lawyers learn the ropes.
paras.zh: 因此，人工智能正在挑战法律职业赖以建立的一些假设，迫使公司重新评估律师如何分配时间、如何收费以及新律师如何熟悉情况。

paras.en: Some of the U.K.'s biggest firms are already putting this into practice. A&O Shearman has worked with legal AI company Harvey to develop artificial intelligence agents for tasks, including reviewing loan agreements and analyzing regulatory filings, which it says can complete in minutes work that previously took several hours. Slaughter and May, meanwhile, has rolled out Harvey across all practice areas this year, including for regulatory research and document analysis.
paras.zh: 英国一些最大的公司已经将其付诸实践。 A&O Shearman 与合法的人工智能公司 Harvey 合作，开发人工智能代理来执行任务，包括审查贷款协议和分析监管文件，据称这些任务可以在几分钟内完成以前需要几个小时的工作。与此同时，司力达今年已在所有业务领域推出 Harvey，包括监管研究和文件分析。

paras.en: The billable hour is central to the business model of many law firms, but when AI significantly reduces the time lawyers spend sifting through and drafting documents, the economics are no longer so straightforward.
paras.zh: 计费时间是许多律师事务所商业模式的核心，但当人工智能显着减少律师筛选和起草文件的时间时，经济学就不再那么简单了。

paras.en: "You can't charge 16 hours for something that takes 16 seconds," Nick Rowles-Davies, founder and CEO of legal finance fund Lexolent, based in London and Dubai, told CNBC.
paras.zh: 总部位于伦敦和迪拜的法律金融基金 Lexolent 的创始人兼首席执行官 Nick Rowles-Davies 告诉 CNBC：“你不可能为需要 16 秒的事情充电 16 小时。”

paras.en: About one in five firms that have widely adopted AI report difficulty meeting billable-hour targets, according to Clio's report. Globally, senior legal leaders expect the share of work charged by the hour to fall from 72% to 44% over the next two to three years, according to a Deloitte survey.
paras.zh: 根据 Clio 的报告，大约五分之一的广泛采用人工智能的公司表示难以实现计费时间目标。德勤的一项调查显示，在全球范围内，高级法律领导者预计未来两到三年内按小时收费的工作比例将从 72% 下降到 44%。

paras.en: Routine work is the most exposed, Rowles-Davies said. "If you've got standard documents and you're just putting in detail, then clearly that's an automatic process."
paras.zh: 罗尔斯-戴维斯说，日常工作是暴露程度最高的。 “如果你有标准文件并且只是提供详细信息，那么显然这是一个自动过程。”

paras.en: But complex legal work still requires human judgment, he added, particularly when interpreting AI output and determining the right strategy for a client.
paras.zh: 但他补充说，复杂的法律工作仍然需要人类的判断，特别是在解释人工智能输出并为客户确定正确的策略时。

paras.en: Lawyers also need to be able to spot AI hallucinations. "There have been a lot of cases where lawyers have been sanctioned for producing briefs before a court with cases that don't exist," Rowles-Davies said.
paras.zh: 律师还需要能够发现人工智能的幻觉。罗尔斯-戴维斯说：“在很多案件中，律师因在法庭上提供不存在的案件摘要而受到制裁。”

paras.en: Mansoor Soomro, who leads the Future of Work Research Unit at Teesside University in Middlesbrough, England, told CNBC the billable hour is certainly not disappearing overnight, but it is getting harder to justify.
paras.zh: 英国米德尔斯堡提赛德大学未来工作研究小组的负责人曼苏尔·苏姆罗 (Mansoor Soomro) 告诉 CNBC，计费工时肯定不会在一夜之间消失，但​​越来越难以证明其合理性。

paras.en: AI is also changing how lawyers learn their trade, Soomro added, as repetitive tasks traditionally helped junior lawyers learn the building blocks of law. Reviewing hundreds of documents taught them what matters, writing up contracts honed their drafting skills and researching dozens of cases helped them develop legal reasoning, he added.
paras.zh: Soomro 补充道，人工智能也正在改变律师学习行业的方式，因为重复性任务传统上可以帮助初级律师学习法律的基础知识。他补充说，审查数百份文件教会了他们什么是重要的，撰写合同磨练了他们的起草技巧，研究数十个案例帮助他们发展了法律推理。

paras.en: As AI takes on more of that work, firms will need to be deliberate about replacing those learning opportunities, according to London-based Jorge Bestard, head of EMEA at Harvey. "A faster route to a draft does not automatically mean a faster route to competence," he told CNBC.
paras.zh: Harvey 欧洲、中东和非洲地区负责人、驻伦敦的豪尔赫·贝斯塔德 (Jorge Bestard) 表示，随着人工智能承担更多此类工作，企业将需要深思熟虑地取代这些学习机会。 “更快的选秀之路并不一定意味着更快的胜任之路，”他告诉 CNBC。

paras.en: A&O Shearman is placing more value on "curiosity and entrepreneurship," said Francesca Bennetts, the firm's London-based head of legal talent. It is also building career paths in legal engineering, product and AI delivery that "barely existed a few years ago," she told CNBC.
paras.zh: A&O Shearman 驻伦敦的法律人才主管 Francesca Bennetts 表示，该公司更加重视“好奇心和创业精神”。她告诉 CNBC，该公司还在法律工程、产品和人工智能交付领域打造“几年前几乎不存在”的职业道路。

paras.en: "The need to develop exceptional lawyers doesn't go away," Bennetts said. "They are the partners and experts of the future."
paras.zh: “培养优秀律师的需求不会消失，”贝内茨说。 “他们是未来的合作伙伴和专家。”

paras.en: Soomro expects judgment to become "disproportionately valuable" in the sector, with lawyers spending more time checking and challenging AI's output and interpreting what it means for a client.
paras.zh: Soomro 预计，判断力在该领域将变得“不成比例地有价值”，律师会花更多时间检查和质疑人工智能的输出，并解释它对客户的意义。

paras.en: "The future may therefore not belong to the lawyer who knows the most about one narrow area, but to the lawyer who knows how to connect multiple areas to solve a complex client problem," he said.
paras.zh: “因此，未来可能不属于最了解某一狭窄领域的律师，而是属于知道如何连接多个领域以解决复杂的客户问题的律师，”他说。

paras.en: Whether AI efficiencies ultimately make lawyers' working lives better may depend on what firms do with the time they get back. Clio's report found that 51% of legal professionals work evenings, but only 32% want to, while 22% work weekends compared with 11% who would choose to. Joshua Lenon, Clio's New York-based lawyer-in-residence, believes some lawyers are already seeing the benefits.
paras.zh: 人工智能的效率最终是否能让律师的工作生活变得更好，可能取决于公司在回来后做什么。 Clio 的报告发现，51% 的法律专业人士在晚上工作，但只有 32% 的人愿意这样做，而 22% 的人在周末工作，而愿意这样做的人为 11%。克里奥纽约常驻律师约书亚·列农 (Joshua Lenon) 认为，一些律师已经看到了其中的好处。

paras.en: "Lawyers [are] telling us that their day is getting better," Lenon told CNBC, as AI becomes more commonplace. "People are really looking at these tools and saying, 'This is making work better.'"
paras.zh: 莱农告诉 CNBC：“律师们告诉我们，随着人工智能变得越来越普遍，他们的日子越来越好。” “人们确实在关注这些工具并说，‘这让工作变得更好。’”

articles.title: The world needs Ukraine’s grain. Its farmers are running out of reasons to plant

paras.en: Ukraine's harvest season is moving from wheat and barley into corn, soybeans and sunflower, and farmer Oleksandr Chumak has had a strong yield so far. That should be good news.
paras.zh: 乌克兰的收获季节正在从小麦和大麦转向玉米、大豆和向日葵，农民 Oleksandr Chumak 迄今为止产量很高。这应该是个好消息。

paras.en: Instead, after 11 years of growing a range of crops in the Odesa region of southern Ukraine, Chumak has had enough.
paras.zh: 相反，在乌克兰南部敖德萨地区种植各种农作物 11 年后，楚马克已经受够了。

paras.en: Storage facilities across both Ukraine and Russia are filled with millions of tons of produce that would normally be sent to Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Africa — but are instead trapped in the warring countries.
paras.zh: 乌克兰和俄罗斯的储存设施里装满了数百万吨的农产品，这些农产品通常会被运往欧洲、中东、亚洲和非洲，但却被困在交战国家。

paras.en: Russian drone and missile hits on Black Sea targets intensified over the summer and into fall, making it impossible to insure commercial ships. Kyiv's retaliatory attacks mean Russian exports are now also stuck, further squeezing global supply.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯无人机和导弹对黑海目标的打击在夏季和秋季加剧，导致商船无法获得保险。基辅的报复性袭击意味着俄罗斯的出口现在也陷入困境，进一步挤压了全球供应。

paras.en: And with fatal Black Sea attacks continuing into October, prospects of a ceasefire look slim, even as Turkey ramps up efforts to broker a deal due to the risk to global food security.
paras.zh: 由于致命的黑海袭击持续到十月，停火的前景看起来很渺茫，尽管土耳其因全球粮食安全面临风险而加大了斡旋协议的力度。

paras.en: Chumak says that around 80% of his grain cannot currently be sold at a profit, and he is out of cash.
paras.zh: Chumak 说，他大约 80% 的粮食目前无法以盈利方式出售，而且他没有现金。

paras.en: A collapse in domestic prices is giving farmers like him little reason to sow for the 2027 crop in the coming months.
paras.zh: 国内价格暴跌让像他这样的农民没有理由在未来几个月播种 2027 年的作物。

paras.en: "For the farmers, it's very difficult because we need to pay taxes, we need to pay rent for land, and now we are not able to do this because we are not able to sell anything," said Andrii Dykun, chairman of the Ukrainian Agri Council.
paras.zh: “对于农民来说，这非常困难，因为我们需要纳税，需要支付土地租金，但现在我们无法做到这一点，因为我们无法出售任何东西，”乌克兰农业委员会主席安德里·戴昆（Andrii Dykun）说。

paras.en: "The only crops we are able to sell are rapeseeds and sunflower seeds. But still, the volume is not enough... So why should we plant if today we have no profits at all?"
paras.zh: “我们唯一能卖的作物是油菜籽和葵花籽。但数量仍然不够……那么，如果今天我们根本没有利润，我们为什么还要种植呢？”

paras.en: "If our stocks will be full, it makes no sense to do any farm operations in the spring because then it's just a waste of time and money."
paras.zh: “如果我们的库存已满，那么在春季进行任何农场作业就没有意义，因为那样只是浪费时间和金钱。”

paras.en: PrivatBank, Ukraine's biggest lender, told CNBC that it had disbursed 1.53 billion hryvnia ($34.2 million) in working capital finance to agribusinesses between June and August, more than double the 718 million hryvnia lent in the same period last year. Small and medium-sized producers account for 70% of its agricultural loan book.
paras.zh: 乌克兰最大的银行 PrivatBank 向 CNBC 表示，6 月至 8 月期间，该公司已向农业企业支付了 15.3 亿格里夫纳（合 3,420 万美元）的营运资金，是去年同期发放的 7.18 亿格里夫纳的两倍多。中小型生产者占其农业贷款的70%。

paras.en: "Funds effectively remain tied up in grain inventories, while farms still need to cover their ongoing operating expenses and secure financing for the autumn and spring sowing campaigns," said Yevhen Zaihraiev, chief corporate and SME business officer at state-owned PrivatBank.
paras.zh: 国有私人银行首席企业和中小企业业务官叶夫亨·扎赫拉耶夫(Yevhen Zaihraiev)表示：“资金实际上仍然与粮食库存挂钩，而农场仍需要支付持续的运营费用，并为秋季和春季播种活动确保融资。”

paras.en: "We are seeing different strategies among our clients. Some agricultural producers are selling their crops sooner, even at less attractive prices, in order to maintain sufficient operating liquidity. Others, particularly those with access to storage capacity, are postponing sales in anticipation of more favorable market prices," he said by email.
paras.zh: “我们看到客户采取了不同的策略。一些农业生产商正在更快地出售农作物，即使价格不太有吸引力，以保持充足的运营流动性。其他农业生产商，特别是那些拥有储存能力的生产商，正在推迟销售，以期获得更有利的市场价格，”他在电子邮件中表示。

paras.en: Ukrainian production of grains and oilseeds is forecast to increase to 85 million tonnes from 80 million tonnes this year, but carry-over stocks from the previous season are pressuring Ukraine's storage infrastructure and logistics, Zaihraiev noted. Those facilities include long plastic silobags snaking across fields and towering metal grain elevators that are themselves increasingly vulnerable to military strikes.
paras.zh: 扎赫拉耶夫指出，预计今年乌克兰谷物和油籽产量将从 8000 万吨增至 8500 万吨，但上一季的结转库存正在给乌克兰的仓储基础设施和物流带来压力。这些设施包括蜿蜒穿过田野的长塑料筒仓和高耸的金属谷物升降机，这些升降机本身越来越容易受到军事打击。

paras.en: "We are also seeing agricultural producers gradually revise their planting plans for next year in favor of oilseeds and niche crops, whose prices are less dependent on logistics costs," Zaihraiev added.
paras.zh: 扎伊赫拉耶夫补充道：“我们还看到农业生产者逐渐修改明年的种植计划，转而种植油籽和利基作物，这些作物的价格不太依赖物流成本。”

paras.en: Farmer Oleksandr Chumak said he will follow that strategy, significantly scaling back planting for next year, avoiding corn and barley altogether, and instead opt for crops which require less fertilizer — which is also facing a global squeeze following amid the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.
paras.zh: 农民 Oleksandr Chumak 表示，他将遵循这一策略，大幅减少明年的种植规模，完全避免种植玉米和大麦，而是选择需要较少化肥的作物——在美以与伊朗的战争之后，这些作物也面临着全球性的挤压。

paras.en: Meanwhile, for Ukrainian farmers — those not currently being drafted to serve — the war with Russia is ever-present. "We are living and working in a place where any time you or your circle can be hit by [a] rocket or drone," Chumak said by phone. "We are sleeping in beds with explosions 300 to 1,000 metres around."
paras.zh: 与此同时，对于乌克兰农民——那些目前尚未被征召入伍的农民来说——与俄罗斯的战争始终存在。 “我们生活和工作的地方，任何时候你或你的圈子都可能被火箭或无人机击中，”丘马克在电话中说。 “我们睡在床上，周围300到1000米处都有爆炸。”

paras.en: Ukraine's agricultural sector has faced farm takeovers, mines and labor shortages ever since Russia's full-scale assault began in early 2022. International bodies have struggled to preserve its export routes through various agreements, including the collapsed Black Sea initiative and the European Union's politically contentious "Solidarity Lanes."
paras.zh: 自俄罗斯于 2022 年初开始全面进攻以来，乌克兰的农业部门一直面临着农场接管、矿山和劳动力短缺的问题。国际机构一直在努力通过各种协议来保护其出口路线，包括失败的黑海倡议和欧盟在政治上存在争议的“团结通道”。

paras.en: Now, the situation inside the country and the consequences for global food chains are the most severe they have been since the war began.
paras.zh: 现在，该国境内的局势以及对全球食物链的影响是自战争开始以来最严重的。

paras.en: Between them, Ukraine and Russia supplied the world with more than half of its sunflower oil, nearly a fifth of its barley and 14% of its wheat in the years leading up to the war, according to the UN. Ukraine is also one of the world's biggest growers of corn, with China and the European Union among its biggest buyers.
paras.zh: 据联合国称，在战争爆发前的几年里，乌克兰和俄罗斯向世界供应了一半以上的葵花籽油、近五分之一的大麦和 14% 的小麦。乌克兰也是世界上最大的玉米种植国之一，中国和欧盟是其最大的买家。

paras.en: Around 90% of Ukraine's main agricultural exports typically run via the Black Sea. In August this year, its grain and legume exports totalled 981,000 tonnes, down about 58% year on year.
paras.zh: 乌克兰约 90% 的主要农产品出口通常通过黑海进行。今年8月份，粮食和豆类出口总量为98.1万吨，同比下降约58%。

paras.en: The risk is heightened by weakness elsewhere. Europe is expected to have a particularly poor corn harvest and needs larger imports just as its demand for feed remains high. The United States is also facing a weaker corn crop.
paras.zh: 其他地区的疲软加剧了这一风险。预计欧洲玉米收成特别差，需要大量进口，同时其饲料需求仍然很高。美国也面临着玉米产量疲软的问题。

paras.en: For now, better wheat and barley crops in Canada, Australia and Argentina, along with good harvests in the Middle East and North Africa, are cushioning the blow.
paras.zh: 目前，加拿大、澳大利亚和阿根廷的小麦和大麦收成较好，加上中东和北非的丰收，正在缓解这一冲击。

paras.en: The continued blockage is supporting commodity prices outside of Russia and Ukraine, but the reopening of Black Sea ports would unleash a wave of cheap supply that would "flip the market fast... with little warning," said Benoit Fayaud, senior manager for grains and oilseeds analysis at Expana.
paras.zh: Expana谷物和油籽分析高级经理Benoit Fayaud表示，持续的封锁正在支撑俄罗斯和乌克兰以外的大宗商品价格，但黑海港口的重新开放将释放一波廉价供应，这将“在几乎没有任何警告的情况下迅速扭转市场”。

paras.en: A deal which restores Ukrainian and Russian exports could see grains prices in other origins decrease by a few dozen dollars, he told CNBC. "They have such big stocks it will be bearish for the market all over the world," he added.
paras.zh: 他告诉 CNBC，恢复乌克兰和俄罗斯出口的协议可能会导致其他产地的谷物价格下降几十美元。 “他们拥有如此大的股票，这对全世界市场来说都是利空的，”他补充道。

paras.en: Prices for Russian and Ukrainian wheat, barley, oilseeds and other products have become so low within the countries that it has intensified the scramble to find alternative routes via rail, road and river, according to Fayaud.
paras.zh: 法约表示，俄罗斯和乌克兰小麦、大麦、油籽和其他产品的价格在这些国家内变得如此之低，以至于加剧了寻找铁路、公路和河流替代路线的争夺。

paras.en: But these alternative routes are "difficult and slow from both countries," he said.
paras.zh: 但他说，这些替代路线“对两国来说都是困难且缓慢的”。

paras.en: Ukraine's Eastern European neighbors such as Poland and Romania are resisting a push to allow grain to transit through them — even temporarily — due to concerns about a glut destroying demand for their own crops.
paras.zh: 乌克兰的东欧邻国，如波兰和罗马尼亚，正在抵制允许粮食通过它们过境的推动——即使是暂时的——因为担心供应过剩会破坏对本国农作物的需求。

paras.en: Another option via the Danube river has been hampered by low water levels; and a key bridge out of Ukraine has been damaged. There are options to export via the Baltic states and through Georgia by land into the Middle East and Central Asia, but this can only cover a small portion of typical flows, Fayaud said.
paras.zh: 另一种经由多瑙河的选择因水位较低而受到阻碍。乌克兰境内的一座重要桥梁已受损。法约表示，可以选择通过波罗的海国家和格鲁吉亚通过陆路出口到中东和中亚，但这只能覆盖典型流量的一小部分。

paras.en: Andrii Dykun of the Ukrainian Agri Council stressed that there was no alternative to the Black Sea routes when it came to pricing.
paras.zh: 乌克兰农业委员会的 Andrii Dykun 强调，在定价方面，除了黑海航线之外别无选择。

paras.en: "It would always be cheaper for us, even for the farmers on the western border of Ukraine, to sell the grain to other ports from Black Sea ports because it's much more profitable for the farmers than to sell it via the border to [the] EU," he said.
paras.zh: 他说：“对我们来说，即使是对乌克兰西部边境的农民来说，从黑海港口向其他港口出售谷物总是更便宜，因为对农民来说，这比通过边境向欧盟出售更有利可图。”

paras.en: "So without Black Sea ports, it will not work for us at all."
paras.zh: “因此，如果没有黑海港口，它对我们来说根本不起作用。”

articles.title: One doctor’s fight to make IUD placement better

paras.en: Rachel Feltman: For Scientific American’s Science Quickly, I’m Rachel Feltman.
paras.zh: 雷切尔·费尔特曼：《科学美国人》的《科学快报》，我是雷切尔·费尔特曼。

paras.en: Intrauterine devices, more commonly known as IUDs, are some of the most effective forms of birth control options available. These small, T-shaped devices are placed directly into the uterus by way of the cervix, where they’re more than 99 percent effective at preventing pregnancy for years at a time. And copper IUDs, which rely on copper ions instead of hormones to limit sperm movement and egg fertilization, are also more than 99 percent effective as emergency contraception if placed within five days of unprotected sex.
paras.zh: 宫内节育器（通常称为宫内节育器）是最有效的节育方法之一。这些小型 T 形装置通过子宫颈直接放入子宫，一次避孕的有效率超过 99%，可持续数年。铜宫内节育器依靠铜离子而不是激素来限制精子运动和卵子受精，如果在无保护性行为后五天内放置，作为紧急避孕的有效率也超过 99%。

paras.en: But while IUDs are a set-it-and-forget-it solution, they do require a visit to the doctor for placement and eventual removal—and that process can be uncomfortable or even quite painful. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention now recommends that doctors counsel patients on pain medication options before an IUD insertion, but there’s not a lot of data out there about effective treatments. Options offered can include local anesthetic creams or injections directly to the cervix, conscious sedation or even full anesthesia—but there’s no real consensus on which intervention to use or how helpful some of them might be.
paras.zh: 但是，虽然宫内节育器是一种一劳永逸的解决方案，但它们确实需要去看医生才能放置并最终取出，而这个过程可能会很不舒服，甚至非常痛苦。美国疾病控制与预防中心现在建议医生在放置宫内节育器之前建议患者选择止痛药，但目前还没有大量关于有效治疗方法的数据。提供的选择包括局部麻醉药膏或直接注射到子宫颈、清醒镇静甚至全身麻醉，但对于使用哪种干预措施或其中一些干预措施的帮助程度尚未达成真正的共识。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Today’s guest is the author of a recent study on a new method for mitigating the potential pain of IUD insertion. Helena Kopp Kallner is a professor at the Karolinska Institute in Sweden and senior consultant in obstetrics and gynecology at the Danderyd Hospital.
paras.zh: 今天的嘉宾是最近一项关于减轻宫内节育器插入潜在疼痛的新方法的研究的作者。海伦娜·科普·卡尔纳 (Helena Kopp Kallner) 是瑞典卡罗林斯卡学院教授、丹德吕德医院妇产科高级顾问。

paras.en: Thank you so much for coming on to chat with us today.
paras.zh: 非常感谢您今天接受我们的采访。

paras.en: Helena Kopp Kallner: Thank you for having me.
paras.zh: 海伦娜·科普·卡尔纳：谢谢你邀请我。

paras.en: Feltman: So you recently published a study on IUD insertion, but before we get into the research itself, I would love to give our listeners a little bit of context about IUDs. So could you tell us a little bit about what makes them such a great birth control option, but also what, you know, the potential downsides are that might keep some patients from getting them?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：您最近发表了一项关于放置宫内节育器的研究，但在我们进入研究本身之前，我很乐意向我们的听众介绍一些有关宫内节育器的背景信息。那么您能否告诉我们一些是什么让它们成为如此出色的节育选择，以及您知道的潜在缺点是什么可能会阻止一些患者获得它们？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: So the very big upside with intrauterine contraception or IUDs is that they are user independent. So that means that you don’t have to think about taking something daily, weekly, monthly, or every three months. So it’s a type of fit-and-forget contraception, as we call it. That means that you have it placed, and then you don’t have to think about it. And, for some IUDs now, you can actually use them for up to eight or 10 years.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：因此宫内避孕或宫内节育器的最大优点是它们独立于用户。因此，这意味着您不必考虑每天、每周、每月或每三个月服用一些东西。因此，正如我们所说，这是一种“一劳永逸”的避孕方法。这意味着你已经把它放置好了，然后你就不必考虑它了。而且，对于现在的一些宫内节育器，您实际上可以使用它们长达八年或十年。

paras.en: They’re also very, very effective, so perfect for young and highly fertile women who don’t wanna become pregnant just now. And for the hormonal IUDs, there’s also an upside with, like, reduction in menstrual flow, so you don’t bleed so much, and also reduction in menstrual pain. So those are the major upsides. But then the downside is that they can be painful to have fitted.
paras.zh: 它们也非常非常有效，非常适合现在不想怀孕的年轻且生育能力强的女性。对于激素宫内节育器来说，还有一个好处，比如可以减少月经量，这样就不会流血太多，也可以减轻经痛。这些是主要的优点。但缺点是安装它们可能会很痛苦。

paras.en: Feltman: Hmm. So tell me about, uh, how your new study came about?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯。那么请告诉我，呃，你的新研究是如何进行的？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: Well, actually, this has been quite a long process, as it usually is with clinical trials. But this was actually an idea that I had myself as I was fitting a lot of IUDs for very young women because I see a lot of very young women in my clinic with a lot of menstrual pain, and they are autistic, and they have lots of different issues. And I was just thinking that I needed to find something simple, so just like, “Okay, why don’t I just, like, inject some, local anesthetic through this, like, very, very thin catheter?” And then I was like, “Okay, now I have to do a study,” because I, I felt it worked. But then we started using a lower concentration of the same substance that we have been using now, and we did the pilot trial with around 80 patients. And then we got, like, near significance, and it was so annoying. And then we planned a larger study, so that’s what we have done now, and then we used a higher concentration of the local anesthetic. And it turned out that it, it works.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：嗯，实际上，这是一个相当漫长的过程，就像临床试验通常一样。但这实际上是我自己的一个想法，因为我为非常年轻的女性安装了很多宫内节育器，因为我在诊所看到很多非常年轻的女性有很多月经疼痛，她们患有自闭症，有很多不同的问题。我只是想我需要找到一些简单的东西，所以就像，“好吧，我为什么不通过这个非常非常细的导管注射一些局部麻醉剂呢？”然后我想，“好吧，现在我必须做一项研究，”因为我，我觉得它有效。但后来我们开始使用现在使用的相同物质的浓度较低，并在大约 80 名患者中进行了试点试验。然后我们就变得接近意义了，这太烦人了。然后我们计划进行一项更大规模的研究，所以这就是我们现在所做的，然后我们使用了更高浓度的局部麻醉剂。事实证明，它确实有效。

paras.en: Feltman: So, prior to you trying this method, what pain relief and mitigation options were available to people getting IUDs inserted?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么，在您尝试这种方法之前，对于放置宫内节育器的人来说，有哪些疼痛缓解和缓解方案？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: I think the most common method still worldwide is just the use of anti-inflammatory drugs like ibuprofen and paracetamol that you take before the IUD insertion, although there are so many trials that have shown that this is not effective.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：我认为世界范围内最常见的方法就是在放置宫内节育器之前服用布洛芬和扑热息痛等抗炎药物，尽管有很多试验表明这并不有效。

paras.en: It works fine for pain after the placement or insertion, but not prophylactically. I think the second most common method is probably to use what we call a paracervical block. So that’s an injection with local anesthetic into the tissue with a needle, which is given on both sides of the cervix and then numbs the cervix and the uterus. But it has also been shown in studies that that method in itself is painful. So usually gynecologists and midwives are a bit reluctant to use that method because they feel that in a lot of patients you actually cause more pain with what’s supposed to cure the pain than what actually causes the pain. We only use it for those who really feel they need it or where we really feel like this is going to be painful.
paras.zh: 它对于缓解放置或插入后的疼痛效果很好，但不能起到预防作用。我认为第二种最常见的方法可能是使用我们所说的宫颈旁阻滞。这是用针将局部麻醉剂注射到子宫颈两侧的组织中，然后麻醉子宫颈和子宫。但研究也表明，这种方法本身是痛苦的。因此，妇科医生和助产士通常不太愿意使用这种方法，因为他们觉得，对于很多患者来说，实际上，治疗疼痛的方法比实际引起疼痛的方法造成的疼痛更多。我们只将它用于那些真正觉得需要它或者我们真的觉得这会很痛苦的人。

paras.en: Feltman: Right. Well, and, it’s occurring to me, I’m, unfortunately intimately familiar with why IUD insertion is painful. But, for people listening who have never had an IUD, could you walk us through what the process of insertion actually is, and, and why there is so much opportunity for discomfort and even pain?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：对。嗯，而且，不幸的是，我突然想到为什么宫内节育器插入会很痛苦。但是，对于那些从未使用过宫内节育器的听众，您能否向我们介绍一下放置宫内节育器的实际过程，以及为什么会有如此多的机会出现不适甚至疼痛？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: Well, I mean, the highest scientific standard of insertion of an IUD is to use, first of all, you use a speculum. That speculum, it visualizes the cervix because the IUD has to be inserted through the cervix into the uterus. So you visualize the cervix, and in some places you also clean the cervix. We don’t do that much in Europe, but in the U.S. it’s usually done, with an antiseptic. And then because the uterus is actually a curved organ, and you’re going to insert something straight into a curved organ, so you have to straighten it out. And, I think a lot of people have a lot of fear of the straightening process because usually that’s done with a so-called tenaculum. And the tenaculum is a very evil-looking kind of instrument with two claws that you, sort of, put onto the cervix. And for some women they don’t feel a thing. It’s not painful. And for others, this is very painful.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：嗯，我的意思是，插入宫内节育器的最高科学标准是使用，首先，你使用窥器。该窥器可以使子宫颈可视化，因为宫内节育器必须通过子宫颈插入子宫。因此，您可以想象子宫颈，并且在某些地方还可以清洁子宫颈。我们在欧洲不做那么多，但在美国通常会使用防腐剂。然后因为子宫实际上是一个弯曲的器官，你要把一些东西直接插入弯曲的器官，所以你必须把它拉直。而且，我认为很多人对拉直过程非常恐惧，因为通常这是用所谓的手杖完成的。触手是一种看起来非常邪恶的工具，有两个爪子，可以放在子宫颈上。对于一些女性来说，她们没有任何感觉。这并不痛苦。而对于其他人来说，这是非常痛苦的。

paras.en: And then after that, usually, you use a so-called sound, which is also a, kind of, a straight instrument, and you use that to measure the length of the cervix and the uterus so that you are sure that you put the IUD up into, like, the bottom of the uterus. And that can also be painful. So you put the sound into the uterus, and then after that you do the IUD insertion.
paras.zh: 然后，通常，您会使用所谓的声音，这也是一种直仪器，然后用它来测量子宫颈和子宫的长度，以便您确定将宫内节育器放入子宫底部。这也可能是痛苦的。因此，您将声音放入子宫，然后进行宫内节育器插入。

paras.en: And the IUD insertion has basically three painful parts of it. First of all is when you put the IUD insertion tube through what’s called the inner os. That’s the upper part of the cervix, and that is a very pain-sensitive part of the uterus.
paras.zh: 宫内节育器插入基本上有三个痛苦的部分。首先是将宫内节育器插入管穿过所谓的内口。这是子宫颈的上部，也是子宫中对疼痛非常敏感的部分。

paras.en: And then, uh, you release the arms of the IUD. So that means that the arms, they’re folded in into the insertion tube, and then when you release the arms, that can also be painful because the IUD suddenly becomes bigger, so it sort of distends the uterine cavity a bit. And that can also be painful.
paras.zh: 然后，呃，你松开宫内节育器的手臂。这意味着手臂被折叠到插入管中，然后当你释放手臂时，这也会很痛苦，因为宫内节育器突然变大，所以它会稍微扩张子宫腔。这也可能是痛苦的。

paras.en: And then there is the final part of it, and that is when you actually push those arms that you’ve just distended, you push them up into the top of the uterus. Now, all of this, it sounds like it takes a lot of time because I’m, I’m speaking slow. But this is a really fast process. So all in all, from the very start to the very finish, if you have a good provider, this is going to take, like, less than a minute total. But it can be a very painful minute.
paras.zh: 然后是最后一部分，那就是当你真正推动刚刚扩张的手臂时，你将它们推入子宫顶部。现在，所有这些，听起来好像需要很多时间，因为我，我说得很慢。但这是一个非常快的过程。总而言之，从开始到结束，如果您有一个好的提供商，那么总共需要不到一分钟的时间。但这可能是非常痛苦的一分钟。

paras.en: Feltman: Right. And it, it seems like for a procedure that’s so common and that potentially causes so much discomfort and frightens people, there aren’t many options, certainly not options that are easy and worthwhile for providers to implement to deal with that pain. Why do you think there’s that gap?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：对。而且，对于一个如此常见、可能会导致如此多的不适和吓到人们的手术来说，似乎没有太多选择，当然也没有提供者可以轻松且值得实施来应对这种痛苦的选择。您认为为什么会有这样的差距？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: So first of all, I think that the, the pain has largely been ignored because it’s a very short-lasting pain in most instances. And secondly, it’s only until the few last years that we have really been starting to insert a lot of IUDs in women who have not had children before.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：首先，我认为这种疼痛在很大程度上被忽视了，因为在大多数情况下，这种疼痛是一种非常短暂的疼痛。其次，直到最近几年，我们才真正开始在以前没有生育过的女性身上放置大量宫内节育器。

paras.en: And we know that women who have had children, especially who have given birth vaginally, that they have less pain than those who never have. And IUDs have traditionally been used for women who have completed their family. But now we inserted a lot of them in the very young for the obvious reasons that I stated in the beginning, that it’s a very effective method and long-lasting, so it’s very suitable for young women.
paras.zh: 我们知道，生过孩子的女性，尤其是阴道分娩的女性，比从未生过孩子的女性承受的疼痛要少。宫内节育器传统上用于已完成家庭的女性。但现在我们在很小的时候就植入了很多，原因很明显，我在开头说过，这是一种非常有效的方法，而且持久，所以非常适合年轻女性。

paras.en: And that, of course, has also brought this pain issue more to the attention of providers and women. So I think that there has been a lack of research, and recently there have been a lot of trials investigating different methods for pain relief with IUD insertions, but they have either been found ineffective or painful in themselves.
paras.zh: 当然，这也让这一疼痛问题更多地引起了医疗服务提供者和女性的关注。所以我认为一直缺乏研究，最近有很多试验研究不同的放置宫内节育器来缓解疼痛的方法，但它们要么被发现无效，要么本身很痛苦。

paras.en: And there are a lot of methods out there used, and people tell me, like, “No, but you should have been doing this, and you should have been doing that. And I do this, and that works fine for me.” And I’m like, “Yes, but have you done the actual study? How do you know that it actually works? Perhaps it’s just, like, placebo that you’re offering to patients.” And I think women deserve more. Women deserve a method that has actually been proven to be effective in a study so that they know that they’re just not being offered placebo. And if you think that your method is so great then do the study. Show the women that it is effective. That is what I have been doing, and I’m actually very proud of that.
paras.zh: 人们使用了很多方法，人们告诉我，“不，但你应该这样做，你应该这样做。我这样做，这对我来说效果很好。”我说，“是的，但是你做过实际的研究吗？你怎么知道它确实有效？也许这只是你向患者提供的安慰剂。”我认为女性应该得到更多。女性应该得到一种在研究中被证明有效的方法，这样她们就知道她们只是没有得到安慰剂。如果您认为您的方法很棒，那么就进行研究。向女性展示它是有效的。这就是我一直在做的事情，我实际上为此感到非常自豪。

paras.en: Feltman: Just anecdotally, I feel like people who I know or, you know, who I, I talk to because of my line of work, I think there’s so much fear, there often is so much actual discomfort and pain. People are so used to it being brushed aside that to some extent I think a provider offering anything goes such a long way into making a patient at least feel calmer. But to your point, how much better to have something that’s been empirically proven to actually help you.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：有趣的是，我觉得我认识的人，或者，你知道，因为我的工作而与我交谈的人，我认为有很多恐惧，经常有很多实际的不适和痛苦。人们已经习惯了它被抛在一边，在某种程度上，我认为提供任何东西的提供者至少可以让病人感到更平静。但就你的观点而言，拥有一些经过经验证明可以真正帮助你的东西有多好。

paras.en: Feltman: So let’s talk a little bit about the method that you tested. You mentioned that it’s a very small catheter. So just so our listeners understand since that, that might not be a word that they hear a lot in their, their everyday lives. Uh, so there’s no injection that’s being used to apply a local anesthetic. Is that correct?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：那么让我们来谈谈您测试的方法。你提到这是一个非常小的导管。因此，我们的听众应该明白，这可能不是他们在日常生活中经常听到的一个词。呃，所以没有使用注射来进行局部麻醉。这是正确的吗？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: That is definitely correct. So this is a very, very thin, plastic catheter. And of course, maybe I should have looked up what it is in inches, but it’s 1.3 millimeters wide. So, it’s a very tiny catheter.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：这绝对是正确的。这是一个非常非常薄的塑料导管。当然，也许我应该查一下它的单位是英寸，但它有 1.3 毫米宽。所以，这是一个非常小的导管。

paras.en: Feltman: So small that translating it to be inches would be meaningless. At that small, I think, I think most people in the U.S. would agree millimeters is much more useful.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：太小了，翻译成英寸是没有意义的。我想，在这么小的情况下，我想大多数美国人都会同意毫米更有用。

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: Oh, great. It’s also, like, extremely soft, so you can completely bend it in either direction. What I usually do is I, I show the catheter to the women when it’s still in its little package. And I say, “See how thin it is,” and then I bend it so that they see that it’s not sharp or anything.
paras.zh: 科普·卡尔纳：哦，太棒了。它也非常柔软，所以你可以向任一方向完全弯曲它。我通常做的是，当导尿管还在小包装中时，我就把导尿管展示给女性看。我说，“看看它有多薄”，然后我将它弯曲，以便他们看到它不锋利或任何东西。

paras.en: And this little catheter is then attached to a syringe with the 10 milliliters of the mepivacaine then, which is the local anesthetic that we use. And so it just like, it slips into the uterus very nicely actually.
paras.zh: 然后将这个小导管连接到装有 10 毫升甲哌卡因（我们使用的局部麻醉剂）的注射器上。所以它实际上非常好地滑入子宫。

paras.en: And what happens then is that this fluid, it just, slowly runs out of the cervix, and it forms like a little puddle inside the vagina, and it sort of, like, drenches the cervix in this local anesthetic fluid. And then we apply the tenaculum to that part of the cervix that has been in the puddle, so to speak.
paras.zh: 然后发生的事情是，这种液体慢慢地从子宫颈流出，在阴道内形成一个小水坑，就像将子宫颈浸入局部麻醉液中一样。然后我们将触手套在子宫颈上水坑里的部分，可以这么说。

paras.en: So perhaps it actually numbs the cervix as well. But that, we haven’t really studied so much. We got, in the pilot trial that I spoke about with the lower concentration of the mepivacaine, there we saw that the absolutely most painful part of the whole procedure was the actual placement of the IUD.
paras.zh: 所以也许它实际上也会使子宫颈麻木。但我们还没有真正研究过那么多。在我谈到的较低浓度甲哌卡因的试点试验中，我们发现整个过程中绝对最痛苦的部分是宫内节育器的实际放置。

paras.en: So then we actually took away the pain assessment for the tenaculum and the, uh, the sounding because the most painful part was the IUD insertion.
paras.zh: 因此，我们实际上取消了对执手的疼痛评估和，呃，声音，因为最痛苦的部分是宫内节育器插入。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, and speaking of that pain assessment, could you tell us about the results? You know, what kind of improvements did you see? And also what kind of feedback did you get from patients about efficacy?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。好吧，说到疼痛评估，您能告诉我们结果吗？您知道，您看到了哪些改进？您从患者那里得到了哪些关于疗效的反馈？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: Yeah, so we measured pain uh, two different ways. First was on what is called the visual analog scale. It’s a 10-centimeters long line. And then the women had the pain scoring sheet, the visual analog scale, this 10 centimeter line in front of them during the IUD insertion.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：是的，所以我们用两种不同的方式测量疼痛。首先是所谓的视觉模拟量表。这是一条10厘米长的线。然后，在放置宫内节育器期间，女性面前会出现疼痛评分表、视觉模拟量表、这条 10 厘米的线。

paras.en: And then we told them, like, “Okay, now you need to score,” and they scored. And it was like, “Now you need to score,” and they scored. So it was, like, an immediate pain assessment. So it’s not like something, like, “Oh, 10 minutes after I thought like, you know, I experienced this kinda thing I remember.” So it’s a very exact kind of pain assessment. So it’s from the absolute worst pain imaginable—sort of like, what if somebody were to saw off your legs with a really rusty saw and you had no anesthesia—to, like, you wake up in the morning, you’re completely pain free, the sun is shining. You score in between those.
paras.zh: 然后我们告诉他们，“好吧，现在你需要得分”，他们就得分了。就像，“现在你需要得分”，他们得分了。所以这就像是即时的疼痛评估。所以这不像是“哦，十分钟后我想，你知道，我经历过我记得的这种事情。”所以这是一种非常精确的疼痛评估。所以它是从你能想象到的绝对最严重的疼痛——有点像，如果有人用一把生锈的锯子锯掉你的腿，而你没有麻醉——到你早上醒来，你完全没有疼痛，阳光明媚。你的得分介于两者之间。

paras.en: And then we also asked women if the pain was tolerable. What is then tolerable? Well, that is subjective to you. Some people might think, like, “Oh, you know, this sawing off of the leg, well, that might be tolerable.” Very few, of course, feel that. And I think that maybe it’s not like the visual analog pain scale really that matters to the patient. What matters to the patient is that you walk out of there and you thought like, “This was okay.” “This was tolerable.” And what we could see was that we lowered the pain score, uh, in the visual analog scale.
paras.zh: 然后我们还询问女性是否可以忍受疼痛。那么什么是可以容忍的呢？嗯，这对你来说是主观的。有些人可能会想，“哦，你知道，把腿锯掉，好吧，这可能是可以忍受的。”当然，很少有人有这种感觉。我认为也许视觉模拟疼痛量表对患者来说并不重要。对病人来说重要的是，当你走出那里时，你会想：“没关系。” “这是可以忍受的。”我们可以看到的是，我们降低了视觉模拟量表中的疼痛评分。

paras.en: But we also raised the proportion of individuals who thought that the pain was tolerable to 98.3%, I think it was. So that means that the absolute vast majority went out of the room with an okay experience, and I think that is the most important thing. Because what, what I think that we see in social media is we, you know, we see, like, women screaming or posting “This was the absolute worst experience I’ve ever had in my life.” We need to lower the proportion of women who have that just absolutely excruciating, painful, intolerable experience.
paras.zh: 但我们也将认为疼痛可以忍受的个体比例提高到了 98.3%，我认为是这样。所以这意味着绝对绝大多数人走出房间时都获得了良好的体验，我认为这是最重要的事情。因为我认为我们在社交媒体上看到的是我们，你知道，我们看到的是，女人尖叫或发帖“这绝对是我一生中经历过的最糟糕的经历。”我们需要降低经历过这种绝对令人难以忍受、痛苦、难以忍受的经历的女性比例。

paras.en: Feltman: Well, and is this a method that other practitioners could implement right now? Is there anything stopping a clinician from reading your study and offering this to their patients?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：嗯，这是其他从业者现在可以实施的方法吗？有什么因素阻止临床医生阅读您的研究并将其提供给患者吗？

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: No, I think this is enough. I mean we have, uh, now performed basically three studies with around 600 randomized individuals with this method. I mean, this is the highest level of evidence. It’s been consistent, the findings throughout all these trials.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：不，我认为这已经足够了。我的意思是，呃，我们现在基本上用这种方法对大约 600 名随机个体进行了三项研究。我的意思是，这是最高级别的证据。所有这些试验的结果都是一致的。

paras.en: And there have been no complications. No increased risk of infection has been seen. So I think just go ahead and implement this. And, if we have patients listening to this, I sincerely ask you to ask for this method because I think that doctors are hard to convince to try something new.
paras.zh: 并且没有出现任何并发症。没有发现感染风险增加。所以我想继续实施这个。而且，如果我们有病人在听这个，我真诚地请你询问这种方法，因为我认为医生很难说服他们尝试新的东西。

paras.en: But if patients start asking for it, like, “Oh, I want this evidence-based pain relief,” and the doctor goes like, “Oh, what is that?” And they’re like, “Oh, do I have to educate you?” So I think that when we educate women, when we educate our patients, that’s when change happens more rapidly.
paras.zh: 但如果病人开始要求它，比如，“哦，我想要这种基于证据的止痛药，”医生就会说，“哦，那是什么？”他们会说，“哦，我必须教育你吗？”所以我认为，当我们教育女性、教育患者时，变革就会发生得更快。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, thank you so much, uh, for coming on to talk to us today. This has been really great.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。嗯，非常感谢您今天来接受我们的采访。这真的很棒。

paras.en: Kopp Kallner: Oh, thank you for having me.
paras.zh: Kopp Kallner：哦，谢谢你邀请我。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for this week on Science Quickly. We’ll be back on Monday with our usual news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是本周 Science Quick 的全部内容。我们将在周一带着我们通常的新闻综述回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: How Hurricane Isaias got so dangerously strong so fast

paras.en: Just one day ago Hurricane Isaias was a Category 1 hurricane. Overnight, it ballooned into a major Category 3 storm with 120-mile-per-hour winds and is set to slam into the U.S. Gulf Coast Friday evening with “life-threatening storm surge,” “devastating winds” and the potential for tornadoes, according to the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).
paras.zh: 就在一天前，飓风伊萨亚斯还是 1 级飓风。据美国国家海洋和大气管理局 (NOAA) 称，它一夜之间升级为 3 级强风暴，风速为每小时 120 英里，并将于周五晚上袭击美国墨西哥湾沿岸，带来“危及生命的风暴潮”、“毁灭性的大风”和潜在的龙卷风。

paras.en: So how did this storm get so dangerous so quickly?
paras.zh: 那么这场风暴为何如此迅速地变得如此危险呢？

paras.en: For one, Isaias’s presence alone is something of an anomaly. As Scientific American previously reported, Isaias is the first hurricane to form in the Atlantic region this season, setting a record for the latest first arrival of any hurricane since satellite monitoring began.
paras.zh: 首先，以赛亚斯的存在本身就是一种反常现象。正如《科学美国人》此前报道的那样，伊萨亚斯是本季在大西洋地区形成的第一场飓风，创下了自卫星监测开始以来最新飓风首次到来的记录。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Meteorologists say Isaias’s late formation is largely because of the presence of El Niño, a pattern of unusually warm ocean waters in the eastern Pacific Ocean that can alter weather patterns across the planet. During El Niño years, hurricane activity in the Atlantic typically drops thanks to choppy wind conditions in the atmosphere, or increased vertical wind shear.
paras.zh: 气象学家表示，伊萨亚斯形成较晚，很大程度上是由于厄尔尼诺现象的存在，厄尔尼诺现象是东太平洋异常温暖的海水模式，可以改变全球的天气模式。在厄尔尼诺现象期间，由于大气中风势汹涌或垂直风切变增加，大西洋的飓风活动通常会下降。

paras.en: But when that wind shear happens to weaken, any burgeoning storm can quickly grow wherever there’s abundant warm ocean water. And there is plenty of that in the Gulf right now.
paras.zh: 但当风切变减弱时，只要有丰富的温暖海水，任何正在形成的风暴都会迅速增长。现在海湾地区就有很多这样的情况。

paras.en: And the storm may have particularly gotten a boost from a large, deep warm-water eddy in the Gulf of Mexico, hurricane specialist Michael Lowry wrote on Substack. This blob of exceptionally warm water formed by spinning off of the Gulf’s Loop Current that is notorious for boosting hurricane strength. The eddy is giving Isaias a “second wind” as it nears landfall, Lowry wrote.
paras.zh: 飓风专家迈克尔·洛瑞 (Michael Lowry) 在 Substack 上写道，这场风暴可能特别受到墨西哥湾一个巨大的深温水涡流的推动。这团异常温暖的水是由墨西哥湾环流旋转形成的，因增强飓风强度而臭名昭著。洛瑞写道，当伊萨亚斯接近登陆时，涡流给它带来了“第二次风”。

paras.en: Warm ocean water fuels tropical cyclones, explains Kim Wood, an associate professor of hydrology and atmospheric sciences at the University of Arizona. “The warmer ocean waters are, the more energy is available, especially if those waters are warm through a deep layer,” Wood says. As a storm’s wind pushes the ocean’s surface water, water deeper down swells up to replace it, they add. If that water is warm—as it would be in this eddy—it can serve as “a longer-lasting energy source” for the storm.
paras.zh: 亚利桑那大学水文学和大气科学副教授金·伍德解释说，温暖的海水助长了热带气旋。伍德说：“海水越温暖，可用的能量就越多，特别是当这些海水深层变暖时。”他们补充说，当风暴的风推动海洋表层的水时，更深处的水就会膨胀并取代它。如果水是温暖的——就像在这个漩涡中一样——它可以作为风暴的“更持久的能源”。

paras.en: A hurricane warning—meaning hurricane conditions are expected—is in effect for parts of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida, with wind, rain and flooding risks expected throughout the wider Gulf Coast region, including in Louisiana and Georgia, and well inland, NOAA predicts. Isaias isn’t expected to weaken until after it makes landfall.
paras.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局(NOAA)预测，密西西比州、阿拉巴马州和佛罗里达州的部分地区将收到飓风警报（意味着预计将出现飓风状况），预计整个墨西哥湾沿岸地区（包括路易斯安那州和佐治亚州以及内陆地区）将面临风、雨和洪水风险。预计伊萨亚斯在登陆之前不会减弱。

paras.en: Gulf Coasters in Isaias’s path should look out for local guidance on how to prepare for the storm’s arrival, including any potential evacuation orders, according to NOAA.
paras.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局表示，伊萨亚斯路径上的墨西哥湾沿岸乘客应留意当地有关如何为风暴到来做好准备的指南，包括任何潜在的疏散命令。

articles.title: Major earthquake strikes Panama—damage and injuries are expected

paras.en: A major earthquake struck Panama on Friday afternoon, but how many people have been affected remains unclear.
paras.zh: 周五下午，巴拿马发生大地震，但有多少人受到影响仍不清楚。

paras.en: The quake struck at 12:56 P.M. local time and was initially measured as an 8.0 magnitude by the U.S. Geological Survey, but that was later downgraded slightly to a 7.7. The quake struck around nine miles (14 kilometers) southwest of Pitaloza Arriba, a small village in Panama’s Herrera Province. Around 4.6 million people experienced moderate to severe shaking, according to the USGS, and potentially strong aftershocks could follow.
paras.zh: 地震发生在中午 12 点 56 分。当地时间，美国地质调查局最初测得震级为 8.0 级，但后来略微下调至 7.7 级。地震发生在巴拿马埃雷拉省的一个小村庄皮塔洛萨阿里巴西南约 9 英里（14 公里）处。据美国地质调查局称，约 460 万人经历了中度至重度震动，随后可能会发生强烈余震。

paras.en: On social media, Panamanian President José Raúl Mulino said he had given instructions to mobilize personnel, resources and aid to the area.
paras.zh: 巴拿马总统何塞·劳尔·穆利诺在社交媒体上表示，他已指示向该地区调动人员、资源和援助。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: No statistics on injuries or deaths have yet been released. The affected area has a relatively low population density.
paras.zh: 目前尚未公布受伤或死亡的统计数据。受影响地区人口密度相对较低。

paras.en: While the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s Tsunami Warning System had initially warned that the quake could pose a tsunami threat in Costa Rica, El Salvador, Peru, Mexico, Guatemala, Nicaragua, Colombia and Ecuador as well as Panama, as of Friday afternoon the alert was no longer in effect.
paras.zh: 虽然美国国家海洋和大气管理局的海啸预警系统最初警告称，此次地震可能对哥斯达黎加、萨尔瓦多、秘鲁、墨西哥、危地马拉、尼加拉瓜、哥伦比亚、厄瓜多尔以及巴拿马构成海啸威胁，但截至周五下午，该警报已不再有效。

paras.en: The threat of tsunami has likely largely receded, says USGS seismologist Susan Hough, as the quake occurred on land and happened at a relatively shallow depth.
paras.zh: 美国地质调查局地震学家苏珊·霍夫表示，海啸的威胁可能已基本消退，因为地震发生在陆地上，且发生在相对较浅的深度。

paras.en: “Because this was on land and shallow, you’re not on the seafloor, so it didn’t move the seafloor underneath the water column, and that’s what you need to generate a tsunami,” she says.
paras.zh: “因为这是在陆地上而且很浅，所以你不在海底，所以它不会移动水柱下方的海底，而这正是引发海啸所需要的，”她说。

paras.en: Shallow earthquakes do lead to more shaking being felt at the surface, though. USGS modeling put the likely casualties in the range of dozens to hundreds of fatalities and damages in the hundreds of millions dollars.
paras.zh: 不过，浅层地震确实会导致地表感受到更多的震动。美国地质勘探局的模型显示，可能的伤亡人数为数十人至数百人，损失达数亿美元。

paras.en: The U.S. embassy in Panama did warn U.S. citizens in the area to avoid damaged structures, as well as the coast, and to monitor local emergency broadcasts for updates.
paras.zh: 美国驻巴拿马大使馆确实警告该地区的美国公民避开受损的建筑物和海岸，并监视当地紧急广播以获取最新消息。

paras.en: Panama is located near the intersection of several major tectonic plates. To the south are the Cocos and Nazca plates, with the Caribbean plate to the north and the South American plate to the east.
paras.zh: 巴拿马位于几个主要构造板块的交汇处附近。南部是科科斯板块和纳斯卡板块，北部是加勒比板块，东部是南美板块。

paras.en: “It was a shallow lateral fault, what we call strike-slip, so similar to the San Andreas,” Hough says.
paras.zh: “这是一个浅层横向断层，我们称之为走滑，与圣安德烈亚斯断层非常相似，”霍夫说。

paras.en: While the meeting place of tectonic plates can lead to the formation of subduction zones, areas where the denser plate is forced underneath the light plate into Earth’s mantle, which can lead to powerful earthquakes as pressure builds, Hough said the subduction zones near Panama don’t meet, which is why the country usually experiences less powerful quakes.
paras.zh: 霍夫表示，虽然构造板块的交汇处可能会导致俯冲带的形成，但密度较大的板块被迫在轻板块下方进入地幔，随着压力的增大，这可能会导致强烈的地震，巴拿马附近的俯冲带不会相遇，这就是为什么该国通常会经历不太强烈的地震。

paras.en: “There’s a complicated zone of faulting that’s at that juncture, and so this earthquake was on one of those faults,” she says. “It was quite large compared to other earthquakes that have been seen in that area.”
paras.zh: “当时有一个复杂的断层带，所以这次地震发生在其中一个断层上，”她说。 “与该地区发生的其他地震相比，这次地震相当大。”

articles.title: Astronomers say they’ve spotted the first miniature quasar pointed at Earth
articles.author: Meghan Bartels

paras.en: Astronomers may have spotted a fun-sized version of one of the brightest and most mysterious cosmic objects. An elusive microblazar, a scaled-down form of the giant, ravenous black holes that haunt the distant universe, seems to have cropped up in our own Milky Way galaxy.
paras.zh: 天文学家可能已经发现了最亮、最神秘的宇宙物体之一的有趣大小的版本。一种难以捉摸的微耀斑，是徘徊在遥远宇宙中的巨大、贪婪的黑洞的缩小版，似乎出现在我们的银河系中。

paras.en: Even more intriguingly, the exotic object may explain the longstanding mystery of how some of the highest-energy particles in the universe came to be, researchers report in a forthcoming paper in Astronomy & Astrophysics.
paras.zh: 更有趣的是，研究人员在《天文学与天体物理学》即将发表的一篇论文中报告说，这个奇异的物体可能解释了宇宙中一些最高能量粒子是如何形成的长期谜团。

paras.en: Blazars are a particular form of quasars, supermassive black holes whose gravity pulls surrounding material into a whirling disk. In this extreme environment, the quasar flings superheated material out in a pair of jets like the axle of a wheel. A blazar is any quasar that points one of its jets approximately toward Earth.
paras.zh: 耀变体是类星体的一种特殊形式，是一种超大质量黑洞，其重力将周围的物质拉入旋转的圆盘中。在这种极端的环境中，类星体像轮轴一样将过热的物质以一对射流的形式喷射出来。耀变体是指其喷流大致指向地球的任何类星体。

paras.en: Astronomers haven’t found quasars or blazars anywhere near Earth, but for nearly 35 years they have hunted for miniature ones in the Milky Way. Such a microquasar consists of a small black hole devouring a large star and sending jets of material spewing out into space. Because they are so much smaller than quasars, material falls into them faster than their massive counterparts.
paras.zh: 天文学家尚未在地球附近发现类星体或耀变体，但近 35 年来他们一直在银河系中寻找微型类星体或耀变体。这样的微类星体由一个小黑洞组成，该黑洞吞噬了一颗大恒星并将物质喷射到太空中。因为它们比类星体小得多，所以物质落入它们的速度比类星体大。

paras.en: “What takes days or weeks to change in a microblazar would take thousands of years in a supermassive blazar,” says astrophysicist Pedro Luque-Escamilla of the University of Jaén in Spain. “It’s a perfect scale model where we can watch a ‘cosmic movie’ in fast-forward.”
paras.zh: 西班牙哈恩大学的天体物理学家佩德罗·卢克·埃斯卡米拉说：“在微耀变体中需要几天或几周才能发生的变化，在超大质量耀变体中则需要数千年的时间。” “这是一个完美的比例模型，我们可以快进地观看一部‘宇宙电影’。”

paras.en: Luque-Escamilla and his colleague Josep Martí have spent two decades hunting for these hyperactive objects in archival telescope data, with little success. “We found many candidates in the past,” Martí says. “They turned out to be extragalactic objects,” full-sized and slower-changing.
paras.zh: 卢克-埃斯卡米拉和他的同事何塞普·马蒂花了二十年的时间在档案望远镜数据中寻找这些异常活跃的天体，但收效甚微。 “我们过去找到了很多候选人，”马蒂说。 “它们原来是河外天体”，尺寸真实且变化缓慢。

paras.en: The pair’s luck changed as they pored over a 1983 catalog produced by a Dutch-American spacecraft and spotted an object referred to as IRAS 18293−0941. When Martí and his colleague cross-referenced this catalog with modern observations by radio telescopes, they saw a small but very bright emission with additional light coming from only one side. That’s “the fingerprint of blazars,” Martí says.
paras.zh: 当他们仔细研究由荷兰-美国航天器制作的 1983 年目录并发现一个名为 IRAS 18293−0941 的物体时，他们的运气发生了变化。当马蒂和他的同事将这个星表与现代射电望远镜的观测结果进行交叉引用时，他们看到了一种微小但非常明亮的发射，并且仅从一侧发出了额外的光。马蒂说，这就是“耀变体的指纹”。

paras.en: The researchers assumed that, like their previous candidates, IRAS 18293−0941 was a full-sized blazar from beyond the Milky Way. But they were intrigued enough to keep investigating. The team ultimately used data from three different observatories on Earth and in space to pinpoint the location as inside our galaxy after all.
paras.zh: 研究人员假设，与之前的候选者一样，IRAS 18293−0941 是来自银河系以外的全尺寸耀变体。但他们对此很感兴趣，继续调查。该团队最终使用了来自地球和太空三个不同天文台的数据来确定该位置毕竟在我们的银河系内部。

paras.en: “The authors took a truly multi-wavelength approach, making use of all different types of astrophysical data from many telescopes,” says astrophysicist Alexandra Tetarenko of the University of Lethbridge in Canada, who was not involved in the new research. “This is not only what distinguishes this work from past claims on other microblazar candidates but also makes it far more convincing.”
paras.zh: “作者采用了真正的多波长方法，利用了来自许多望远镜的所有不同类型的天体物理数据，”加拿大莱斯布里奇大学的天体物理学家亚历山德拉·泰塔伦科（Alexandra Tetarenko）说道，她没有参与这项新研究。 “这不仅是这项工作与过去对其他微火体候选者的主张的区别，而且也使其更具说服力。”

paras.en: The scientists also noticed that IRAS 18293−0941 was quite near a known patch of ultrahigh energy particles — particles with energy 100 times higher than the Large Hadron Collider can create, that scientists have struggled to explain what could juice them up to such extremes.
paras.zh: 科学家们还注意到，IRAS 18293−0941 非常接近一片已知的超高能粒子——能量比大型强子对撞机产生的能量高 100 倍，科学家们一直在努力解释是什么让它们达到如此极端的水平。

paras.en: Martí and his colleagues argue this isn’t a coincidence: the “hotspot” marks where the microblazar’s invisible jet pointing away from Earth slams into a cloud of matter, acting as a massive particle accelerator. The team is already working to gather additional observations of the proposed hotspot.
paras.zh: 马蒂和他的同事认为这并非巧合：“热点”标志着微耀体的不可见射流远离地球撞击物质云，充当了一个巨大的粒子加速器。该团队已经在努力收集对拟议热点的更多观察结果。

paras.en: The hotspot observations, as well as observations of the visible jet, should both give scientists a better understanding of the microblazar’s dramatic capacities, Luque-Escamilla says, as if the universe made a special particle accelerator just for scientists. “It’s like comparing a high-tech human laboratory to a supreme cosmic engine,” he says.
paras.zh: 卢克-埃斯卡米拉说，热点观测以及可见射流观测都应该让科学家更好地了解微耀体的巨大能力，就好像宇宙专门为科学家制造了一个特殊的粒子加速器一样。 “这就像将高科技人类实验室与至高无上的宇宙引擎进行比较，”他说。

articles.title: Remember the ‘caregiving kills’ study? Reality is more nuanced
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: When social and affective neuroscientist Naomi Eisenberger’s dad developed dementia, she knew the popular wisdom. Caring for him could shave years off her life. But Eisenberger, of UCLA, was skeptical. Caring for her dad, who died in January, was stressful but also meaningful, she says. “It gave me a lot of joy to bring him some happiness.”
paras.zh: 当社会和情感神经科学家内奥米·艾森伯格的父亲患上痴呆症时，她知道流行的智慧。照顾他可能会缩短她的寿命。但加州大学洛杉矶分校的艾森伯格对此表示怀疑。她说，照顾一月份去世的父亲很有压力，但也很有意义。 “给他带来一些快乐让我感到非常高兴。”

paras.en: Caregiving kills as an idea first emerged in the scientific literature almost three decades ago. Distressed caregivers were 63 percent more likely to die within four years than non-caregivers, psychiatrists Richard Schulz and Scott Beach reported in 1999 in the Journal of the American Medical Association. The finding has since been cited almost 5,300 times, including almost 300 times in the past two years.
paras.zh: 大约三十年前，“看护致死”这一概念首次出现在科学文献中。 1999 年，精神病学家理查德·舒尔茨 (Richard Schulz) 和斯科特·比奇 (Scott Beach) 在《美国医学会杂志》上发表报告称，陷入困境的看护者四年内死亡的可能性比非看护者高出 63%。此后，这一发现被引用了近 5,300 次，其中过去两年被引用了近 300 次。

paras.en: But researchers have largely failed to replicate that finding, with considerable research showing instead that caregiving links with living longer, Eisenberger and colleagues report in September in Biopsychosocial Science and Medicine. Caregiving stress may be softened by humans’ hardwired propensity to help others in need, the researchers suspect.
paras.zh: 但研究人员在很大程度上未能复制这一发现，大量研究表明护理与寿命延长有关，艾森伯格及其同事在 9 月份的《生物心理社会科学与医学》杂志上报告说。研究人员怀疑，人类天生就有帮助有需要的人的倾向，这可能会减轻照顾压力。

paras.en: Silence surrounding caregiving’s positives is probably well-intentioned. In 2025, almost one-quarter of all adults in the United States, some 63 million people, provided care to adults or children with a medical condition or disability, according to a 2025 report by AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Almost 65 percent of caregivers surveyed reported experiencing moderate or high emotional stress and almost half reported financial difficulties. Yet financial and emotional support for caregivers remains limited, the report notes.
paras.zh: 对护理的积极作用保持沉默可能是善意的。根据 AARP 和国家护理联盟 2025 年的一份报告，到 2025 年，美国近四分之一的成年人（约 6300 万人）为患有疾病或残疾的成年人或儿童提供护理。近 65% 的受访护理人员表示面临中度或高度情绪压力，近一半的护理人员表示经济困难。然而报告指出，对护理人员的经济和情感支持仍然有限。

paras.en: Highlighting caregiving’s pros could jeopardize what little help is available, says sociologist and gerontologist Rebecca Utz of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. “I don’t like to take our foot off the pedal and say that caregiving is so positive because it’s hard, and people need support.”
paras.zh: 盐湖城犹他大学的社会学家和老年学家丽贝卡·乌茨 (Rebecca Utz) 表示，强调看护的优点可能会危及现有的有限帮助。 “我不想把我们的脚从踏板上移开，说护理是如此积极，因为它很困难，人们需要支持。”

paras.en: But painting caregiving as wholly negative, rather than nuanced, erases insight into how caregiving might also protect health, Eisenberger and colleagues argue. Most stressors, such as work-related burnout, link with chronic inflammation. Caregiving is less likely to show that link. Understanding that caregiving paradox could reveal how the body can withstand stress, Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: 但艾森伯格和同事认为，将护理描述为完全消极的而非细致入微的，会抹杀护理如何保护健康的见解。大多数压力源，例如与工作相关的倦怠，都与慢性炎症有关。护理不太可能显示出这种联系。艾森伯格说，了解护理悖论可以揭示身体如何承受压力。

paras.en: Moreover, helping a loved one may bring unexpected benefits, Eisenberger says. She cites a 2003 study in The Gerontologist showing that adult children who did not care for a parent with severe disabilities experienced more depression than those who did, though the researchers could not show causation. “I’m not suggesting everyone go out and engage in informal caregiving,” Eisenberger says. “I’m trying to make informal caregiving [feel] a little less scary.”
paras.zh: 此外，艾森伯格说，帮助亲人可能会带来意想不到的好处。她引用了《老年学家》2003 年的一项研究，该研究表明，不照顾父母患有严重残疾的成年子女比那些照顾父母的成年子女更容易患抑郁症，尽管研究人员无法证明其中的因果关系。 “我并不是建议每个人都出去从事非正式护理，”艾森伯格说。 “我正在努力让非正式护理[感觉]不那么可怕。”

paras.en: Caregiving was labeled as life-threatening
paras.zh: 护理被标记为危及生命

paras.en: In highlighting the need for researchers to take caregiver well-being seriously, the 1999 study was groundbreaking, Eisenberger and colleagues write. But it had design flaws.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格及其同事写道，1999 年的研究具有开创性，强调了研究人员认真对待护理人员福祉的必要性。但它存在设计缺陷。

paras.en: Schulz and Beach, both of the University of Pittsburgh, compared mortality rates across a four-year period from over 800 individuals. Roughly half the participants had disabled spouses, with some serving as caregivers and others not; the other half had nondisabled spouses and served as the control. Caregiving spouses filled out self-reports indicating their degree of mental strain.
paras.zh: 匹兹堡大学的舒尔茨和比奇比较了 800 多人在四年内的死亡率。大约一半的参与者有残疾配偶，其中一些担任看护人，另一些则不担任；另一半的配偶没有残疾，作为对照。照顾配偶的配偶填写自我报告，表明他们的精神紧张程度。

paras.en: Over the next four years, 103 participants died. Schulz and Beach zoomed in on mortality rates among one subgroup — spousal caregivers reporting considerable strain. Of those distressed caregivers, 17 percent died during the study period compared with 9 percent of control group members.
paras.zh: 在接下来的四年里，103 名参与者死亡。舒尔茨和比奇重点研究了一个亚群体的死亡率——配偶照顾者报告称压力相当大。在那些陷入困境的护理人员中，有 17% 的人在研究期间死亡，而对照组成员的这一比例为 9%。

paras.en: But buried in the data was another finding, Eisenberger and colleagues note: Individuals not providing care to their disabled spouses still died at the same rate as caregivers experiencing distress. Individuals with sick and healthy spouses occupy different realities, largely invalidating comparisons between those groups, Eisenberger says. In this case, the findings suggest that having a sick or disabled spouse, and not caregiving status, increases one’s likelihood of dying.
paras.zh: 但艾森伯格和同事指出，数据中隐藏着另一个发现：不向残疾配偶提供护理的个人的死亡率仍然与经历痛苦的​​护理人员的死亡率相同。艾森伯格说，配偶患病和健康的人面临着不同的现实，这在很大程度上使这些群体之间的比较无效。在这种情况下，研究结果表明，配偶生病或残疾，而不是照顾状态，会增加一个人的死亡可能性。

paras.en: More than 6,000 caregivers were asked to evaluate both the sense of purpose and emotional stress associated with caregiving. Their answers illustrate the role’s emotional duality.
paras.zh: 超过 6,000 名护理人员被要求评估与护理相关的使命感和情绪压力。他们的回答说明了这个角色的情感二元性。

paras.en: The team is not the first to dispute the idea that caregiving kills. That list includes Schulz himself, who coauthored a 2009 Psychological Science study titled, “Caregiving behavior is associated with decreased mortality risk.” (Neither Schulz nor Beach could be reached for comment.) That study, though, has been cited less than 400 times, with just a couple dozen citations in the past two years.
paras.zh: 该团队并不是第一个对护理致死这一观点提出质疑的团队。该名单中包括舒尔茨本人，他在 2009 年与人合着了一项心理科学研究，题为“看护行为与降低死亡风险相关”。 （无法联系到舒尔茨和比奇发表评论。）不过，该研究被引用的次数不到 400 次，在过去两年中仅被引用了几十次。

paras.en: “I … assumed that the field would have taken notice,” says evolutionary and social psychologist Stephanie Brown, an author on the 2009 paper and a similar 2014 review of caregiving in Social Issues and Policy Review. But “slam pieces on caregiving” remain on prominent display in doctor’s offices and other medical settings, says Brown, of the Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University in New York.
paras.zh: “我……以为这个领域会注意到，”进化和社会心理学家斯蒂芬妮·布朗（Stephanie Brown）说，她是 2009 年这篇论文的作者，也是《社会问题和政策评论》2014 年类似的护理评论的作者。但纽约石溪大学文艺复兴医学院的布朗表示，“有关护理的大肆宣传”仍然在医生办公室和其他医疗场所的显着位置展示。

paras.en: Caregivers are stressed. Biology may help compensate
paras.zh: 照顾者压力很大。生物学可能有助于补偿

paras.en: More recent research hints at why caregiving, a tremendously stressful undertaking, may not kill.
paras.zh: 最近的研究暗示了为什么看护这种压力巨大的工作可能不会致命。

paras.en: It’s increasingly accepted that stress can trigger systemic inflammation that then compromises the immune system. In theory, stressed caregivers should be inflamed. They’re not, researchers reported in 2020 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. That study relied on data from more than 30,000 U.S. adults. In surveys taken in the early 2000s and the 2010s, participants indicated their caregiver status, type and intensity of care being given, and experiences of strain. They also provided blood samples.
paras.zh: 人们越来越认识到，压力会引发全身炎症，进而损害免疫系统。从理论上讲，承受压力的看护者应该会发炎。研究人员在 2020 年《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，事实并非如此。该研究依赖于 30,000 多名美国成年人的数据。在 2000 年代初期和 2010 年代进行的调查中，参与者表明了他们的护理人员状况、护理类型和强度以及紧张经历。他们还提供了血液样本。

paras.en: The scientists zoomed in on roughly 250 people who became regular caregivers and analyzed their blood samples for six inflammation-related biomarkers. Those biomarkers did not go up, on average, when people transitioned to caregiving, the team found. Nor did they go up relative to a matched control group of non-caregivers selected from the larger sample. Those findings held true for even the most stressed caregivers, including spouses caring for a partner with dementia.
paras.zh: 科学家们重点关注了大约 250 名成为定期护理人员的人，并分析了他们的血液样本中的 6 种与炎症相关的生物标志物。研究小组发现，当人们转向护理时，这些生物标记物平均并没有上升。相对于从较大样本中选出的非照顾者的匹配对照组，它们也没有上升。即使是压力最大的护理人员，包括照顾患有痴呆症的伴侣的配偶，这些发现也适用。

paras.en: How, though, are caregivers largely avoiding inflammation associated with chronic stress? “We don’t really know,” says gerontologist and clinical psychologist William Haley of the University of South Florida in Tampa. “There’s a lot of mysteries here.”
paras.zh: 然而，护理人员如何在很大程度上避免与慢性压力相关的炎症呢？ “我们真的不知道，”坦帕南佛罗里达大学的老年学家和临床心理学家威廉·黑利说。 “这里有很多谜团。”

paras.en: Eisenberger and colleagues theorize that the key to the caregiving paradox may lie in a biological system that evolved among mammals to protect offspring that remain helpless well after birth. That “mammalian caregiving system” seems to encourage caring and tamp down the normal stress response that tells people to flee danger, at least when their baby is involved, Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格及其同事推测，照顾悖论的关键可能在于哺乳动物进化出的生物系统，以保护出生后仍无助的后代。艾森伯格说，这种“哺乳动物照顾系统”似乎鼓励照顾并抑制正常的压力反应，这种压力反应告诉人们要逃离危险，至少在涉及婴儿时是这样。

paras.en: Studies primarily in rodents hint at how that caregiving system works, Eisenberger notes. And emerging evidence in humans suggests that this system kicks on even in non-parenting contexts, such as holding onto a partner in pain or giving money to family. In preliminary work, Brown and colleagues even saw signs of it among strangers who bonded during an activity.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格指出，主要针对啮齿类动物的研究揭示了这一护理系统的运作方式。人类身上不断出现的证据表明，即使在非养育子女的情况下，这个系统也会发挥作用，比如在痛苦中抓住伴侣或给家人钱。在初步工作中，布朗和同事甚至在活动期间结识的陌生人中发现了这种迹象。

paras.en: Researchers are missing fascinating questions
paras.zh: 研究人员错过了一些有趣的问题

paras.en: The contradictory feelings Eisenberger experienced while caring for her dad are common. Caregivers can’t disentangle the advantages of the mammalian caregiving system from the strain of helping. Yet over half of caregivers surveyed by AARP reported that caring for a loved one gave them a sense of purpose.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格在照顾父亲时经历的矛盾感受很常见。护理人员无法将哺乳动物护理系统的优势与帮助的压力区分开来。然而，美国退休人员协会 (AARP) 调查显示，超过一半的护理人员表示，照顾亲人给了他们一种使命感。

paras.en: Ironically, minimizing potential positives to protect caregivers may do more harm than good, researchers say. Caregivers may hear only how awful their next several months or years may be. Others might run from the responsibility and later experience regret.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，讽刺的是，为了保护护理人员而最大限度地减少潜在的积极因素可能弊大于利。护理人员可能只会听到他们接下来的几个月或几年可能会多么糟糕。其他人可能会逃避责任，然后感到后悔。

paras.en: “What if we tell people that … helping others can be really fulfilling even if it can be stressful, too?” Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: “如果我们告诉人们......帮助他人可以真正让人感到满足，即使它也可能有压力？”艾森伯格说。

paras.en: Reticence around caregiving’s benefits has also hampered scientists’ ability to advise people undertaking such a difficult role, Eisenberger and colleagues note. Can feeling compassion for a sick loved one turn on the mammalian caregiving system, or does one have to provide care? What if someone has a fraught relationship with the sick family member? Ultimately, when does the stress of opting out of caregiving outweigh the stress of opting in? Framing caregiving as entirely negative means those questions rarely even get asked.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格和同事指出，对护理好处的沉默也阻碍了科学家为承担如此困难角色的人们提供建议的能力。对生病的亲人的同情可以开启哺乳动物的护理系统，还是必须提供护理？如果有人与生病的家庭成员关系紧张怎么办？最终，选择退出护理的压力何时超过选择接受护理的压力？将护理视为完全消极意味着这些问题很少被问到。

articles.title: A quake on Mars may have set these rocks rolling
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Earthquakes frequently trigger rock falls. Now there’s solid evidence marsquakes can send boulders tumbling, too.
paras.zh: 地震经常引发岩石坠落。现在有确凿的证据表明火星地震也会导致巨石翻滚。

paras.en: Scientists mined high-resolution imagery of the Red Planet taken shortly after a recent temblor and found hundreds of new imprints left by tumbling boulders, researchers report September 2 in npj Space Exploration. Such rockfalls can be used as a proxy for seismic data, which is difficult to collect across the solar system.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 2 日在 npj Space Exploration 上报告称，科学家们挖掘了最近一次地震后不久拍摄的这颗红色星球的高分辨率图像，发现了数百个翻滚巨石留下的新印记。这种落石可以用作地震数据的代理，而地震数据很难在整个太阳系中收集。

paras.en: The data were collected with NASA’s InSight lander, which touched down on Mars in 2018. Over the next four years, its seismometer detected more than a thousand marsquakes. Many of those temblors originated in a region known as Cerberus Fossae, just north of the Martian equator. That’s a dynamic landscape riddled with slopes, cracks and rocks on the move, says Vijayan, a planetary scientist at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad, India, who goes by a single name. “Thousands and thousands of boulders have fallen.”
paras.zh: 这些数据是通过 NASA 的 InSight 着陆器收集的，该着陆器于 2018 年登陆火星。在接下来的四年里，其地震仪检测到了一千多次火星地震。许多地震起源于火星赤道以北的一个名为塞伯鲁斯窝的地区。印度艾哈迈达巴德物理研究实验室的行星科学家维贾扬（Vijayan）说，这是一个动态的景观，布满了斜坡、裂缝和移动的岩石。 “成千上万的巨石倒塌了。”

paras.en: Vijayan and his collaborators focused on one well-detected marsquake captured by InSight that occurred in July 2019 just a few tens of kilometers from Cerberus Fossae. By comparing images taken in June 2019 and December 2020, the researchers discovered 27 new linelike features. Each was composed of tens to hundreds of distinct marks. These structures were most likely tracks created by boulders bouncing downhill, the team concluded.
paras.zh: Vijayan 和他的合作者重点研究了 InSight 捕捉到的一场地震，该地震发生在 2019 年 7 月，距离 Cerberus Fossae 仅几十公里。通过比较 2019 年 6 月和 2020 年 12 月拍摄的图像，研究人员发现了 27 个新的线状特征。每个标记都由数十到数百个不同的标记组成。研究小组得出结论，这些结构很可能是巨石下坡时留下的痕迹。

paras.en: Using historical imagery, the researchers calculated that only about two such features form each year on average in Cerberus Fossae. “We have statistics of previous boulder falls,” says Bivas Das, a seismologist at the Physical Research Laboratory and a member of the research team. Recording 27 new structures over a span of just 18 months is wholly unexpected, Das says. “That’s a big increase.” The nearby marsquake recorded by InSight was probably the instigator, the team concluded.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用历史图像计算出，Cerberus Fossae 每年平均只有大约两个这样的特征。 “我们有以前巨石坠落的统计数据，”物理研究实验室的地震学家、研究小组成员比瓦斯·达斯（Bivas Das）说。 Das 表示，在短短 18 个月内记录了 27 个新结构，这完全出乎意料。 “这是一个很大的增长。”研究小组得出结论，洞察号记录的附近的火星地震可能是始作俑者。

paras.en: Mysteries remain, however. All of the rockfalls occurred on the north side of a prominent valley in Cerberus Fossae, despite more boulders being located on the south side of the valley. “That puzzles us,” Vijayan says. The complex landscape of Cerberus Fossae might well alter how seismic waves travel, making it difficult to predict how shaking will impact different areas, he says. “The wave propagation is going to be complicated.”
paras.zh: 然而，谜团依然存在。尽管更多的巨石位于山谷的南侧，但所有落石都发生在塞伯鲁斯窝沟的一个著名山谷的北侧。 “这让我们感到困惑，”维贾扬说。他说，Cerberus Fossae 的复杂景观很可能会改变地震波的传播方式，从而很难预测震动将如何影响不同地区。 “波的传播将会很复杂。”

paras.en: Looking for such boulder falls elsewhere could help space exploration efforts, the team suggests. Human settlements would do best avoiding areas that are seismically active, and tumbling boulders can be the proverbial canaries in the coal mine, Vijayan says. “They’re like a proxy in the absence of seismic data.”
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，在其他地方寻找此类巨石坠落可能有助于太空探索工作。维贾扬说，人类住区最好避开地震活跃的地区，而翻滚的巨石可能是煤矿里众所周知的金丝雀。 “在缺乏地震数据的情况下，它们就像一个代理。”

articles.title: New Trial Compared Muscle Gains in Vegetarians And Meat Eaters. One Difference Stood Out.
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Plant-based diets are associated with many long-term health benefits, but for older adults, there may be a potential downside.
paras.zh: 以植物为基础的饮食与许多长期健康益处相关，但对于老年人来说，可能存在潜在的缺点。

paras.en: Eating a strictly vegetarian diet may make it harder to protect muscle mass as we age.
paras.zh: 随着年龄的增长，严格素食可能会使保护肌肉质量变得更加困难。

paras.en: Protein is a key component in building, maintaining, and strengthening muscle, and in older age, you could need more of it than current guidelines suggest.
paras.zh: 蛋白质是构建、维持和增强肌肉的关键成分，在老年时，您可能需要比当前指南建议的更多的蛋白质。

paras.en: Vegetarians tend to eat less dietary protein than meat eaters, and recent research suggests that underweight vegetarians are less likely to live to 100.
paras.zh: 素食者往往比肉食者吃更少的膳食蛋白质，最近的研究表明，体重过轻的素食者活到 100 岁的可能性较小。

paras.en: Now, a new clinical trial adds a positive spin.
paras.zh: 现在，一项新的临床试验增添了积极的一面。

paras.en: Among adults aged 55 and over, both vegetarians and meat eaters gained muscle and showed similar improvements in strength and physical performance after 12 weeks of resistance training.
paras.zh: 在 55 岁及以上的成年人中，经过 12 周的阻力训练后，素食者和肉食者都获得了肌肉，并且在力量和身体表现方面表现出类似的改善。

paras.en: The findings are published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上。

paras.en: "Importantly, our results also show that a predominantly plant-based diet can still support meaningful improvements in muscle mass, strength, and physical function when protein intake is sufficiently high and combined with resistance training," write researchers at the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences in the Netherlands.
paras.zh: 荷兰阿姆斯特丹应用科学大学的研究人员写道：“重要的是，我们的结果还表明，当蛋白质摄入量足够高并结合阻力训练时，以植物为主的饮食仍然可以支持肌肉质量、力量和身体功能的有意义的改善。”

paras.en: In the randomized trial, 108 adults undertook either a vegetarian diet or an omnivorous diet for three months.
paras.zh: 在这项随机试验中，108 名成年人接受了三个月的素食或杂食饮食。

paras.en: During the trial, they also partook in resistance training three times a week, with exercises including leg presses, squats, chest presses, lat pulldowns, arm pulls, and abdominal exercises.
paras.zh: 试验期间，他们还每周参加3次阻力训练，练习内容包括腿推、深蹲、推胸、背阔肌下拉、手臂拉和腹部练习。

paras.en: Each participant was counseled on healthy eating plans and how to consume at least 1.2 grams of protein per kilogram of their body weight each day.
paras.zh: 每位参与者都被告知健康饮食计划以及如何每天每公斤体重摄入至少 1.2 克蛋白质。

paras.en: On average, both groups were successful in meeting their daily protein goals – even the vegetarians, who could not eat meat or fish, only dairy, eggs, or plant-based proteins.
paras.zh: 平均而言，两组人都成功地实现了每日蛋白质目标——即使是素食者，他们不能吃肉或鱼，只能吃奶制品、鸡蛋或植物性蛋白质。

paras.en: By the end of the trial, muscle strength and physical performance improved in both groups, with no significant difference between vegetarians and meat eaters.
paras.zh: 试验结束时，两组的肌肉力量和身体机能都有所改善，素食者和肉食者之间没有显着差异。

paras.en: On leg presses, participants could lift more weight, and on chair stands, they stood up faster than they did when the trial first started.
paras.zh: 在腿部推举中，参与者可以举起更多的重量，在椅子支架上，他们站起来的速度比试验刚开始时更快。

paras.en: But there was one key difference between the groups.
paras.zh: 但两组之间有一个关键的区别。

paras.en: Muscle mass in the legs and arms increased in both vegetarians and omnivores during the trial, but omnivores showed about 70 percent more gains (+0.66 kilograms, compared to +0.38 kg for vegetarians).
paras.zh: 在试验期间，素食者和杂食者的腿部和手臂肌肉质量均有所增加，但杂食者的肌肉质量增加了约 70%（增加了 0.66 公斤，而素食者则增加了 0.38 公斤）。

paras.en: It is not clear whether this is due to lower protein intake by vegetarians, or something about the quality of dietary protein provided by meat and other animal-based foods.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚这是由于素食者蛋白质摄入量较低，还是与肉类和其他动物性食品提供的膳食蛋白质质量有关。

paras.en: Interestingly, the study found that vegetarians who ate more protein tended to gain more muscle, whereas meat eaters who ate more protein didn't.
paras.zh: 有趣的是，研究发现，吃更多蛋白质的素食者往往会获得更多的肌肉，而吃更多蛋白质的肉食者则不然。

paras.en: "The omnivorous group likely reached a saturating protein threshold where additional intake yielded no further anabolic benefit," the authors hypothesize.
paras.zh: 作者推测：“杂食性群体可能达到了饱和蛋白质阈值，额外摄入不会产生进一步的合成代谢益处。”

paras.en: Nutrition is a highly complex area of research subject to lifestyle, behavioral, genetic, social, and environmental factors too numerous to count.
paras.zh: 营养是一个高度复杂的研究领域，受到生活方式、行为、遗传、社会和环境因素无数的影响。

paras.en: This particular cohort of older adults was predominantly White, healthy, and highly educated. It is unclear if these findings are relevant to others.
paras.zh: 这个特殊的老年人群体主要是白人、健康且受过高等教育。目前尚不清楚这些发现是否与其他发现相关。

paras.en: Still, the results join other recent studies suggesting that vegetarian diets, as long as they provide enough calories and essential nutrients, can be associated with lives as long and as healthy as those of meat eaters.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，这些结果与最近的其他研究相结合，表明素食饮食只要提供足够的热量和必需营养素，就可以与肉食者一样长寿和健康。

paras.en: Research like this is a good reminder that eating enough protein in older age is important, especially for vegetarians.
paras.zh: 这样的研究很好地提醒我们，在老年时摄入足够的蛋白质很重要，尤其是对于素食者来说。

paras.en: "The suitability of a more plant-based diet may depend on individual context," the authors of the new study conclude.
paras.zh: 这项新研究的作者总结道：“以植物为主的饮食是否适合可能取决于个人情况。”

paras.en: "For people with low appetite or low energy intake, extra focus on meeting protein targets and ensuring protein quality is likely needed to maintain muscle mass, which is particularly important for older adults."
paras.zh: “对于食欲低下或能量摄入低的人来说，可能需要额外关注达到蛋白质目标并确保蛋白质质量以维持肌肉质量，这对老年人尤其重要。”

paras.en: The research has been published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《美国临床营养学杂志》上。

articles.title: A Distinct New Type of Diabetes Has Officially Been Recognized
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: After decades of controversy, the International Diabetes Federation (IDF) officially recognized a fifth form of diabetes in 2025.
paras.zh: 经过数十年的争议，国际糖尿病联盟 (IDF) 于 2025 年正式承认第五种糖尿病。

paras.en: It's now urging other health authorities, like the World Health Organization (WHO), to follow suit.
paras.zh: 它现在敦促世界卫生组织（WHO）等其他卫生当局效仿。

paras.en: Type 5 diabetes is rarely discussed or researched, and yet it is thought to impact up to 25 million people worldwide, especially those in low- and middle-income nations where access to medical care is limited.
paras.zh: 5 型糖尿病很少被讨论或研究，但人们认为它影响着全世界多达 2500 万人，特别是那些获得医疗服务有限的低收入和中等收入国家的人。

paras.en: It was first described in 1955 in Jamaica, then forgotten about for many years. Even once it was acknowledged by the WHO in the 1980s, the diagnosis created controversy.
paras.zh: 它于 1955 年在牙买加首次被描述，随后被遗忘多年。即使在 20 世纪 80 年代被世界卫生组织承认后，这一诊断仍然引起了争议。

paras.en: For going on seven decades, scientists have debated whether type 5 diabetes exists at all, and in 1999, WHO withdrew the classification due to a lack of evidence. There has been little agreement on how to diagnose type 5 diabetes or how to treat it.
paras.zh: 七十年来，科学家们一直在争论 5 型糖尿病是否存在，1999 年，世界卫生组织因缺乏证据而撤销了这一分类。关于如何诊断 5 型糖尿病或如何治疗它，目前尚未达成一致意见。

paras.en: Type 1 diabetes is an autoimmune condition that destroys the pancreas's ability to produce insulin. Type 2 diabetes is an insensitivity to insulin due to diet and lifestyle. Type 3c diabetes is commonly caused by damage to the pancreas. Gestational diabetes is triggered by hormonal changes during pregnancy.
paras.zh: 1 型糖尿病是一种自身免疫性疾病，会破坏胰腺产生胰岛素的能力。 2型糖尿病是由于饮食和生活方式而对胰岛素不敏感。 3c 型糖尿病通常是由胰腺损伤引起的。妊娠期糖尿病是由怀孕期间荷尔蒙的变化引发的。

paras.en: Type 5 diabetes seems to stem from nutrient deficiency. Previously known as malnutrition-related diabetes mellitus (MRDM), this form of diabetes is commonly misdiagnosed as other types.
paras.zh: 5 型糖尿病似乎源于营养缺乏。这种糖尿病以前被称为营养不良相关糖尿病 (MRDM)，通常被误诊为其他类型。

paras.en: And yet, because insulin resistance does not seem to be the primary cause of type 5 diabetes, existing treatments may not help. In fact, they may even harm.
paras.zh: 然而，由于胰岛素抵抗似乎并不是 5 型糖尿病的主要原因，现有的治疗方法可能无济于事。事实上，它们甚至可能造成伤害。

paras.en: Watch the clip below for a summary of the announcement:
paras.zh: 观看下面的剪辑，了解该公告的摘要：

paras.en: "Understanding the specific types of diabetes someone has is crucial to providing the right treatment," Craig Beall, a diabetes researcher at the University of Exeter, explained in May 2025.
paras.zh: 埃克塞特大学糖尿病研究人员克雷格·比尔 (Craig Beall) 于 2025 年 5 月解释说：“了解某人所患糖尿病的具体类型对于提供正确的治疗至关重要。”

paras.en: For years now, Meredith Hawkins, an endocrinologist at the Albert Einstein College of Medicine's Global Diabetes Institute, has called for global recognition of type 5 diabetes, which typically impacts people in Asia and Africa who are experiencing severe food insecurity.
paras.zh: 多年来，阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦医学院全球糖尿病研究所的内分泌学家梅雷迪思·霍金斯一直呼吁全球对 5 型糖尿病的认识，这种糖尿病通常会影响亚洲和非洲面临严重粮食不安全的人们。

paras.en: "Malnutrition-related diabetes is more common than tuberculosis and nearly as common as HIV/ AIDS, but the lack of an official name has hindered efforts to diagnose patients or find effective therapies," Hawkins said in 2025.
paras.zh: “与营养不良相关的糖尿病比肺结核更常见，几乎与艾滋病毒/艾滋病一样常见，但缺乏正式名称阻碍了诊断患者或寻找有效疗法的努力，”霍金斯在 2025 年表示。

paras.en: "I'm hopeful that this formal recognition as type 5 diabetes will lead to progress against this long-neglected disease that severely debilitates people and is often fatal."
paras.zh: “我希望，对 5 型糖尿病的正式认可将导致在对抗这种长期被忽视的疾病方面取得进展，这种疾病严重削弱人们的能力，并且往往是致命的。”

paras.en: In recent years, numerous animal and human studies have shown that chronic nutrient deficiencies can have lifelong impacts on the pancreas, disrupting its ability to secrete insulin and balance blood sugar levels.
paras.zh: 近年来，大量动物和人类研究表明，慢性营养缺乏会对胰腺产生终生影响，破坏其分泌胰岛素和平衡血糖水平的能力。

paras.en: Hawkins' own work, published in 2022, was the first to establish a unique metabolic profile for this with malnutrition-related diabetes.
paras.zh: Hawkins 自己的研究成果于 2022 年发表，首次针对营养不良相关的糖尿病建立了独特的代谢特征。

paras.en: She and her colleagues ran a small trial in south India, which showed people with MRDM are insulin-deficient like people with type 1 diabetes, but not to the same degree, and still sensitive to insulin, unlike people with type 2 diabetes who develop resistance.
paras.zh: 她和她的同事在印度南部进行了一项小型试验，结果显示 MRDM 患者与 1 型糖尿病患者一样缺乏胰岛素，但程度不同，并且仍然对胰岛素敏感，这与产生耐药性的 2 型糖尿病患者不同。

paras.en: "Type 5 diabetes stands apart with its unique pathogenesis, theorized to involve compromised pancreatic development resulting from extended periods of nutritional insufficiency," Rahul Garg, a physician at F.H. Medical College and Hospital in India, wrote in a recent review.
paras.zh: 印度 F.H. 医学院和医院的医生 Rahul Garg 在最近的一篇评论中写道：“5 型糖尿病因其独特的发病机制而与众不同，理论上与长期营养不足导致的胰腺发育受损有关。”

paras.en: In light of this evidence, the IDF is making a concerted effort to at last recognize type 5 diabetes.
paras.zh: 鉴于这一证据，IDF 正在齐心协力，最终识别 5 型糖尿病。

paras.en: Some researchers have said the move is "long overdue", while others argue that it is "unwarranted" due to "diagnostic uncertainty" stemming from the variety of diabetes cases seemingly related to malnutrition.
paras.zh: 一些研究人员表示，此举“早就应该”，而另一些研究人员则认为，此举“没有根据”，因为各种糖尿病病例似乎与营养不良有关，导致“诊断不确定性”。

paras.en: Some say the number of patients with type 5 diabetes is growing; others say its prevalence is receding. Either way, it's all tied up in whether the condition is properly diagnosed and recognized.
paras.zh: 有人说，5 型糖尿病患者的数量正在增加；有人说，5 型糖尿病患者的数量正在增加。其他人则表示其流行率正在下降。不管怎样，这都取决于这种情况是否得到正确的诊断和识别。

paras.en: Without a formal name and recognition, it's challenging to fund research, and without further evidence, it's impossible to know enough about a condition to formulate a standard diagnosis or to say how many people it affects.
paras.zh: 如果没有正式的名称和认可，资助研究就很困难，而且如果没有进一步的证据，就不可能对某种疾病有足够的了解来制定标准诊断或说出它影响了多少人。
