paras.en: The German prosecutor's office told me the justice system was outside of any politics. Sabotage is an offence against Germany's constitution.
paras.zh: 德国检察官办公室告诉我，司法系统与任何政治无关。破坏活动是违反德国宪法的行为。

paras.en: Equally frustrating for the Ukrainians I met was their own government's silence.
paras.zh: 对于我遇到的乌克兰人来说，同样令人沮丧的是他们自己的政府的沉默。

paras.en: "At the very minimum, he's a military man, so if there are any questions, they should be addressed to the state, not to him," a close contact of Serhii K complained.
paras.zh: “至少，他是一名军人，所以如果有任何问题，应该向国家提出，而不是向他提出，”Serhii K 的一位密切接触者抱怨道。

paras.en: Ahead of his extradition to Germany, his lawyer here in Italy told me his client had felt "abandoned".
paras.zh: 在他被引渡到德国之前，他在意大利的律师告诉我，他的当事人感到“被抛弃了”。

paras.en: Germany has a whole list of suspects, but only one other name has been revealed so far.
paras.zh: 德国拥有一份完整的嫌疑人名单，但迄今为止只公布了另一个名字。

paras.en: Volodymyr Zhuravlyov is currently fighting extradition from Croatia where he was arrested in August.
paras.zh: 弗拉基米尔·朱拉夫廖夫 (Volodymyr Zhuravlyov) 目前正在争取从克罗地亚引渡他，他于 8 月在克罗地亚被捕。

paras.en: He was there as a consultant on a new thriller film about the Nord Stream blasts, though he denies any role in the real-life operation.
paras.zh: 他在那里担任一部有关北溪爆炸的新惊悚片的顾问，尽管他否认在现实生活中扮演过任何角色。

paras.en: Travelling was a risky move, when he knew Germany was pursuing him.
paras.zh: 当他知道德国正在追捕他时，旅行是一个冒险的举动。

paras.en: Zhuravylov has lived in Warsaw with his family since just before Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine and has his own business there installing air conditioning.
paras.zh: 朱拉维洛夫在俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰之前就与家人一起住在华沙，并在那里拥有自己的空调安装生意。

paras.en: He is also a keen and competent deep-sea diver.
paras.zh: 他也是一位敏锐且能干的深海潜水员。

paras.en: Last year, he was arrested in Warsaw on a warrant issued by Germany but a Polish judge refused to extradite him.
paras.zh: 去年，他根据德国发出的逮捕令在华沙被捕，但波兰法官拒绝引渡他。

paras.en: In a dramatic twist, he ruled instead that a Ukrainian attack on Nord Stream, if that was what happened, would be a "just" act in a "bloody and genocidal war".
paras.zh: 戏剧性的转折是，他裁定乌克兰对北溪的袭击，如果真是这样的话，将是一场“血腥和种族灭绝战争”中的“正义”行为。

paras.en: As one source close to the case put it to me: "The Poles don't like Ukrainians, historically, but they hate Russians and Germans even more."
paras.zh: 正如一位了解此案的消息人士对我说的：“从历史上看，波兰人不喜欢乌克兰人，但他们更讨厌俄罗斯人和德国人。”

paras.en: The implications of this case reach far beyond the courthouse in Hamburg.
paras.zh: 此案的影响远远超出了汉堡法院的范围。

paras.en: After a slow start, Germany is now Ukraine's biggest supplier of military aid. The far-right AfD party, currently riding high in the polls, has seized on the Nord Stream case to bolster its argument that support for Kyiv needs to stop.
paras.zh: 经过缓慢的起步后，德国现在成为乌克兰最大的军事援助提供者。目前民意调查中民调高居不下的极右翼政党选择党抓住北溪案来支持其论点，即需要停止对基辅的支持。

paras.en: It is awkward, at the very least, for the governments in both Berlin and Kyiv.
paras.zh: 至少对于柏林和基辅政府来说，这很尴尬。

paras.en: It also raises questions about what constitutes a legitimate military target: who can hit what, and where, outside an open war zone.
paras.zh: 它还提出了关于什么构成合法军事目标的问题：谁可以在开放战区之外打击什么、什么地方。

paras.en: When asked about the explosions, President Zelensky has previously insisted that Ukraine "definitely didn't do that".
paras.zh: 当被问及爆炸事件时，泽伦斯基总统此前坚称乌克兰“绝对没有这样做”。

paras.en: This week, a foreign ministry spokesman went further.
paras.zh: 本周，外交部发言人更进一步。

paras.en: "I find it very unfortunate that this entire discussion has come to focus on who blew [the pipelines] up, rather than who built them," Heorhii Tykhyi told the BBC, forcefully.
paras.zh: “我发现非常不幸的是，整个讨论都集中在谁炸毁了（管道），而不是谁建造了它们，”Heorhii Tykhyi 有力地告诉 BBC。

paras.en: He argued that the Nord Stream pipelines had "untied Russia's hands" to go to war, because it no longer needed that to transit Ukraine for its gas to reach Europe.
paras.zh: 他认为，北溪管道“解放了俄罗斯的双手”，让俄罗斯不再需要通过乌克兰将天然气输送到欧洲。

paras.en: "Did we warn about this? We did," Tykhyi wanted to know. "Did anyone listen to us? No, no-one did."
paras.zh: “我们有警告过这件事吗？我们警告过，”蒂赫伊想知道。 “有人听我们说话吗？不，没有人听。”

paras.en: Serhii K will shortly become the first suspect to face charges in this high profile trial.
paras.zh: Serhii K 很快将成为这一备受瞩目的审判中第一个面临指控的嫌疑人。

paras.en: Zhuravlyov's case could be merged, in theory, at a later date, though that would be complicated.
paras.zh: 理论上，朱拉夫廖夫的案件可以在以后合并，尽管这会很复杂。

paras.en: Those who know Serhii K call him a patriot.
paras.zh: 认识 Serhii K 的人称他为爱国者。

paras.en: He signed up to defend Ukraine when Russia invaded even though he had several children and was exempt - and fought until December 2023.
paras.zh: 当俄罗斯入侵时，他报名保卫乌克兰，尽管他有几个孩子并且获得豁免，并一直战斗到 2023 年 12 月。

paras.en: His military ID shows that he was still in active service when the pipelines were blown up, meaning someone in Ukraine's military command knew exactly where he was and what he was doing.
paras.zh: 他的军人身份证显示，管道被炸毁时，他仍在现役，这意味着乌克兰军事指挥部的某个人确切知道他在哪里以及在做什么。

paras.en: And in court Serhii K himself will not say a word, either.
paras.zh: 在法庭上，Serhii K 本人也不会说一句话。

paras.en: His legal team will argue that he is not authorised to reveal details of any activities as a soldier and produce sworn statements from two of his military superiors to back that up.
paras.zh: 他的法律团队将辩称，他无权透露作为士兵的任何活动细节，并出示两名军事上级的宣誓声明来支持这一点。

paras.en: I am told one of them will be the man widely named as the mastermind of the entire Nord Stream plot.
paras.zh: 有人告诉我，其中一位将是被广泛称为整个北溪阴谋的策划者的人。

articles.title: Thousands of security personnel deployed as Delhi braces for ‘cockroach’ protest

paras.en: Parts of the Indian capital, Delhi, have been turned into a fortress, with tens of thousands of security forces deployed, as the influential Gen Z-led "cockroach" movement has called for a major protest on Saturday.
paras.zh: 印度首都德里的部分地区已变成堡垒，部署了数万名安全部队，影响力极大的 Z 世代领导的“蟑螂”运动周六呼吁举行大规模抗议。

paras.en: The protesters are seeking electoral reforms and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voters' lists.
paras.zh: 抗议者正在寻求选举改革，并要求首席选举专员 (CEC) 贾内什·库马尔 (Gyanesh Kumar) 因操纵选民名单的指控而辞职。

paras.en: The Election Commission has denied this and Kumar is yet to comment on calls for his resignation.
paras.zh: 选举委员会否认了这一点，库马尔尚未对要求他辞职的呼声发表评论。

paras.en: The protest comes just months after the movement brought thousands of young people onto Delhi's streets in July, in demonstrations that saw violent clashes with police and forced India's education minister to resign.
paras.zh: 就在这次抗议活动发生几个月前，7月份，数千名年轻人走上德里街头，举行示威活动，与警察发生暴力冲突，并迫使印度教育部长辞职。

paras.en: Police say they have denied permission for Saturday's gathering, and all roads leading to Jantar Mantar, the main protest venue, have been closed off with huge metal barricades.
paras.zh: 警方表示，他们拒绝批准周六的集会，所有通往主要抗议地点简塔·曼塔天文台的道路均已被巨大的金属路障封锁。

paras.en: The restrictions have caused major disruption across central Delhi, with traffic diverted from several key roads. A journey that would normally take 15 minutes took more than an hour this morning.
paras.zh: 这些限制对德里市中心造成了严重干扰，几条主要道路的交通被迫分流。原本需要 15 分钟的旅程今天早上却花了一个多小时。

paras.en: At Jantar Mantar, police and paramilitary personnel are stationed behind barricades and ropes, preventing people from entering the protest site. Drones could be seen flying overhead.
paras.zh: 在简塔·曼塔天文台，警察和准军事人员驻扎在路障和绳索后面，阻止人们进入抗议现场。可以看到无人机在头顶飞过。

paras.en: Some protesters who arrived early were stopped and questioned by security personnel. The BBC also saw at least five people being detained near the site.
paras.zh: 一些提前到达的抗议者被安全人员拦住并询问。英国广播公司还看到至少五人在现场附近被拘留。

paras.en: Journalists covering the protest have been cordoned off into a designated area nearby.
paras.zh: 报道抗议活动的记者已被封锁到附近的指定区域。

paras.en: At a nearby roundabout, loudspeakers repeatedly broadcast appeals for people to cooperate with the police.
paras.zh: 在附近的一个环岛，扩音器反复播放呼吁人们与警方合作的呼吁。

paras.en: Delhi Police has defended the measures, saying they were necessary to maintain public safety and prevent overcrowding at Jantar Mantar, which can accommodate only 1,000 people at a time.
paras.zh: 德里警方为这些措施进行了辩护，称这些措施是维护公共安全和防止简塔·曼塔天文台过度拥挤所必需的，该中心一次只能容纳 1,000 人。

paras.en: Several trains to Delhi have also been cancelled and police have ordered dozens of metro stations shut to prevent protesters from gathering.
paras.zh: 几趟开往德里的火车也被取消，警方下令关闭数十个地铁站，以防止抗议者聚集。

paras.en: But Abhijeet Dipke, founder â of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) - the online satirical movement that is spearheading the protests - has said the CJP will march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday morning "come what may".
paras.zh: 但蟑螂人民党 (CJP) 的创始人阿比吉特·迪普克 (Abhijeet Dipke) 表示，“无论如何”，蟑螂人民党将在周六早上向简塔·曼塔天文台游行。

paras.en: "If you want to jail us or even shoot us we are prepared," he added, addressing âPrime Minister Narendra Modi in a post on X.
paras.zh: 他在 X 上的一篇帖子中对总理纳伦德拉·莫迪 (Narendra Modi) 说道：“如果你们想监禁我们，甚至向我们开枪，我们已经做好了准备。”

paras.en: The CJP first emerged as a major protest movement during weeks of demonstrations demanding education reforms over the summer. The resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan in July was seen as a major victory for the group.
paras.zh: 在夏季持续数周的要求教育改革的示威活动中，CJP 首次成为一场重大抗议运动。教育部长 Dharmendra Pradhan 于 7 月辞职被视为该组织的重大胜利。

paras.en: CJP protesters returned to the streets last week with a rally in Mumbai to demand Kumar's resignation. On Thursday, they held another large rally in the southern city of Bengaluru (formerly Bangalore).
paras.zh: 上周，CJP 抗议者重返街头，在孟买举行集会，要求库马尔辞职。周四，他们在南部城市班加罗尔（原班加罗尔）举行了另一场大型集会。

paras.en: Student groups and opposition parties have also protested in the capital over the past few days.
paras.zh: 过去几天，学生团体和反对党也在首都举行抗议活动。

paras.en: Saturday's protests are being billed as the biggest in recent times as they are also being supported by several opposition parties, farmer organisations and student groups.
paras.zh: 周六的抗议活动被称为近年来最大规模的抗议活动，因为它们也得到了一些反对党、农民组织和学生团体的支持。

paras.en: CJP leaders allege the authorities have been preventing many of their supporters from reaching Delhi.
paras.zh: 印度人民党领导人声称当局一直阻止他们的许多支持者到达德里。

paras.en: In the capital, more than 30,000 police and paramilitary personnel have been deployed and authorities have appealed to citizens to stay away from protests.
paras.zh: 在首都，已部署了三万多名警察和准军事人员，当局呼吁公民远离抗议活动。

paras.en: Police official Nupur Prasad told a press conference, external that one of the reasons for denying permission to protest at Jantar Mantar was the "short notice" given by the CJP.
paras.zh: 警察官员努普尔·普拉萨德 (Nupur Prasad) 在对外新闻发布会上表示，拒绝允许在简塔·曼塔天文台举行抗议活动的原因之一是 CJP 发出的“临时通知”。

paras.en: "Under current guidelines, an application to organise an event at Jantar Mantar must be submitted at least 10 days prior to the scheduled date," she said.
paras.zh: “根据目前的指导方针，在简塔·曼塔天文台举办活动的申请必须在预定日期前至少 10 天提交，”她说。

paras.en: Also, she added that in the past, the CJP had not followed "lawful directions" given to them.
paras.zh: 此外，她补充说，过去，CJP 没有遵循给予他们的“合法指示”。

paras.en: "In light of the non-compliance with prescribed procedures, the failure to adhere to past legal directions, and the current state of public safety, law and order, and traffic regulation, permission for the proposed protest at Jantar Mantar is hereby denied."
paras.zh: “鉴于不遵守规定程序、不遵守过去的法律指示以及公共安全、法律和秩序以及交通管制的现状，特此拒绝批准在简塔·曼塔天文台举行拟议的抗议活动。”

paras.en: The CJP have questioned police denying them permission for the protest - they say that legally they only have to inform the police and do not need their approval to gather.
paras.zh: CJP 质疑警方拒绝批准他们举行抗议活动，他们表示，从法律上讲，他们只需要通知警方即可，不需要他们的批准即可集会。

paras.en: At the centre of the row is a controversial revision of the country's electoral rolls known as the Special Intensive Revision, or SIR, which began last year.
paras.zh: 争论的焦点是去年开始的一项有争议的国家选民名册修订，即“特别强化修订”（SIR）。

paras.en: The Election Commission says it is to remove duplicate and ineligible entries - and so far, 130 million names have been struck off the voters' list.
paras.zh: 选举委员会表示将删除重复和不合格的条目——到目前为止，已有 1.3 亿人的名字被从选民名单上删除。

paras.en: But opposition parties and activists have alleged that many of those are eligible voters and that the process is being manipulated by CEC Kumar to favour Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) during elections. Both the BJP and the Election Commission have rejected the accusations.
paras.zh: 但反对党和活动人士声称，其中许多人都是合格选民，而中央选举委员会库马尔正在操纵这一过程，以在选举期间支持莫迪领导的印度人民党（BJP）。印度人民党和选举委员会都否认了这些指控。

paras.en: The past few days have also seen a major escalation in the opposition's standoff with the Election Commission.
paras.zh: 过去几天，反对派与选举委员会的对峙也大幅升级。

paras.en: For three days in a row starting Tuesday, Delhi witnessed dramatic scenes with police breaking up protests by opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and other MPs over the issue.
paras.zh: 从周二开始，德里连续三天出现了警察驱散反对派领导人拉胡尔·甘地和其他议员就此问题举行的抗议活动的戏剧性场面。

paras.en: Videos showing police forcing Gandhi on to a bus and preventing him from climbing out of the bus window subsequently went viral on social media.
paras.zh: 警方强迫甘地登上公交车并阻止他从车窗爬出的视频随后在社交媒体上疯传。

articles.title: Public executions in the US stopped nearly a century ago -  why are they resuming now?

paras.en: They came in their thousands from near and far - men, women and children lined up on a Kentucky riverfront for the public hanging of a black man convicted of raping and killing an elderly white widow.
paras.zh: 成千上万的人从远近赶来——男人、女人和儿童在肯塔基州河边排队，等待公开绞死一名因强奸和杀害老年白人寡妇而被定罪的黑人。

paras.en: It was 14 August 1936 in Owensboro, Kentucky, a sweltering Friday in the middle of a legendary heat wave. Some slept overnight near the gallows to preserve their spots. Others held "necktie" parties the previous evening, arriving hungover as teenagers sold popcorn and soda to the spectators.
paras.zh: 那是 1936 年 8 月 14 日，肯塔基州欧文斯伯勒，一个闷热的星期五，正值传说中的热浪之中。有些人在绞刑架附近过夜，以保留自己的斑点。其他人则在前一天晚上举办了“领带”派对，在宿醉中抵达，青少年们向观众出售爆米花和苏打水。

paras.en: By the execution time of 5am, the crowd had swelled to an estimated 20,000.
paras.zh: 到凌晨 5 点执行死刑时，人群估计已增至 20,000 人。

paras.en: That's when Rainey Bethea, an orphan in his 20s, stepped up to the gallows - sentenced to death after allegedly confessing to robbing, raping and killing Lischia Edwards, 70.
paras.zh: 就在那时，20 多岁的孤儿雷尼·贝西娅 (Rainey Bethea) 走上绞刑架，因涉嫌抢劫、强奸和杀害 70 岁的利斯基亚·爱德华兹 (Lischia Edwards) 而被判处死刑。

paras.en: The previous afternoon, he'd eaten a last meal of fried chicken, pork chops, mashed potatoes, pickled cucumbers, cornbread, lemon pie and ice cream.
paras.zh: 前一天下午，他吃了最后一顿饭，有炸鸡、猪排、土豆泥、腌黄瓜、玉米面包、柠檬派和冰淇淋。

paras.en: Many of those gathered - including press from as far away as Chicago and New York - came to see the rumoured "Lady Executioner;" the local sheriff had died four months earlier, and his widow became the unlikely female replacement. She declined to pull the trip lever herself, however, and it was hired hangmen who instead sent Bethea to his death.
paras.zh: 许多聚集的人——包括远至芝加哥和纽约的媒体——前来一睹传闻中的“刽子手女士”的风采；当地治安官四个月前去世，他的遗孀成为了不太可能的女性替代者。然而，她拒绝亲自拉动解扣杆，而是雇佣了刽子手将贝西娅处死。

paras.en: That moment marked the last high-profile public hanging in America. The circus surrounding Bethea's death embarrassed many in Kentucky, and the governor outlawed public executions 18 months later.
paras.zh: 那一刻标志着美国最后一次高调的公开绞刑。围绕贝西娅之死的闹剧让肯塔基州的许多人感到尴尬，18 个月后，州长宣布公开处决为非法。

paras.en: By then, most states had abolished capital punishment in view of the masses as societal attitudes sought more humane and private methods. Another hanging was attended by a few hundred in Missouri in 1937, but that was lesser known and marked America's final public execution - until now.
paras.zh: 那时，随着社会态度寻求更人道和私人的方法，大多数州已经考虑到大众废除了死刑。 1937 年，密苏里州有数百人参加了另一次绞刑，但那次绞刑鲜为人知，也是美国最后一次公开处决——直到现在。

paras.en: A little more than 90 years after Bethea's killing, US Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced that the military would publicly execute Nidal Hasan, who killed 13 unarmed fellow soldiers in 2009 at the Fort Hood military base in Texas.
paras.zh: 贝西娅被杀 90 多年后，美国国防部长皮特·赫格斯宣布，军方将公开处决尼达尔·哈桑，后者于 2009 年在德克萨斯州胡德堡军事基地杀害了 13 名手无寸铁的战友。

paras.en: The Pentagon followed up by saying the execution by firing squad would be live-streamed.
paras.zh: 五角大楼随后表示，行刑队的处决将进行现场直播。

paras.en: "People need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things," Hegseth said.
paras.zh: “人们需要明白，这类事情会带来严重后果，”赫格斯说。

paras.en: University of Colorado professor emeritus Michael Radelet, a long-time scholar of capital punishment, was shocked.
paras.zh: 长期研究死刑的学者、科罗拉多大学名誉教授迈克尔·拉德莱特（Michael Radelet）感到震惊。

paras.en: "I never imagined [another] public execution," he told BBC.
paras.zh: “我从未想象过（另一次）公开处决，”他告诉英国广播公司。

paras.en: He noted how public support for the death penalty in general has been steadily declining; it was 80% in 1994, for example, but now stands at 52%.
paras.zh: 他指出，公众对死刑的支持总体上正在稳步下降。例如，1994 年这一比例为 80%，但现在为 52%。

paras.en: "It's gone down precipitously, especially when you give the alternative of life without parole," he said.
paras.zh: “它急剧下降，尤其是当你选择不假释的生活时，”他说。

paras.en: It's too soon to know what the American public thinks of the idea of livestreaming an execution. But it's nearly certain that millions or more will tune in.
paras.zh: 现在了解美国公众对直播处决的想法还为时过早。但几乎可以肯定的是，数百万人或更多的人会收听。

paras.en: With Hegseth's announcement, Radelet said, "the justification for the death penalty becomes entertainment â¦ bring your popcorn, invite your friends".
paras.zh: 随着赫格斯的宣布，拉德莱特说，“死刑的理由变成了娱乐……带上你的爆米花，邀请你的朋友”。

paras.en: Sonya Lea, who just last year published a book about Bethea's execution, "felt absolute horror for our descendants" when she heard of the announced firing squad livestream.
paras.zh: 索尼娅·李(Sonya Lea)去年刚刚出版了一本关于贝西娅被处决的书，当她听说行刑队现场直播时，“对我们的后代感到绝对的恐惧”。

paras.en: "What they called it in 1936 was a carnival of sadism," she said. "That we now have the technology that can make it go wider than the 20,000 people who showed up â¦ to witness in Owensboro, Kentucky, it just makes it even more horrific."
paras.zh: “1936 年他们称之为虐待狂的狂欢节，”她说。 “我们现在拥有的技术可以让它传播到比肯塔基州欧文斯伯勒见证的 20,000 人更广泛的范围，这只会让事情变得更加可怕。”

paras.en: Lea's grandparents were teenage newlyweds among that 1936 crowd. She only found out after her grandmother's 2002 death, when she read an account her late grandma had given detailing how they were close enough to hear Bethea's neck snap.
paras.zh: Lea 的祖父母是 1936 年人群中十几岁的新婚夫妇。她是在 2002 年祖母去世后才知道这一点的，当时她读到了已故祖母的一份叙述，其中详细描述了他们是如何靠得足够近，可以听到贝西娅的脖子折断的声音。

paras.en: The author's subsequent years of research taught her that many Kentuckians were "haunted" by that execution.
paras.zh: 作者随后几年的研究告诉她，许多肯塔基州人都被那次处决“困扰”。

paras.en: "I really thought, with all my heart, that we had put this in the rearview mirror, this level of grotesquery that only a few countries in the world engage in - Iran, North Korea, Afghanistan," she said. "Are we now, as the United States of America, considering ourselves to be part of that kind of government? It's just horrific."
paras.zh: 她说：“我真心实意地认为，我们已经把这件事抛诸脑后了，世界上只有伊朗、朝鲜、阿富汗等少数几个国家才会发生这种程度的怪诞事件。” “作为美利坚合众国，我们现在是否认为自己是这种政府的一部分？这太可怕了。”

paras.en: But the polarisation and rhetoric in American politics may have, in some way, perhaps set the stage for such an announcement, said Kurt Gray, a social psychology professor at Ohio State University.
paras.zh: 但俄亥俄州立大学社会心理学教授库尔特·格雷表示，美国政治中的两极分化和言论可能在某种程度上为这一声明奠定了基础。

paras.en: "Some Americans might thirst for blood, but I think a lot of Americans don't, and, if anything, I think a lot of other Americans are just kind of maybe desensitised," he said. "So it's not like they're cheering a public execution; they're just like, 'Oh, yeah, I guess that's where we're at now.'"
paras.zh: 他说：“一些美国人可能渴望鲜血，但我认为很多美国人并不渴求，而且，如果说有什么不同的话，我认为很多其他美国人可能只是麻木了。” “所以他们并不是在为公开处决欢呼；他们只是说，‘哦，是的，我想这就是我们现在的处境。’”

paras.en: Other research indicates that Hegseth and the administration may be reading the country wrong.
paras.zh: 其他研究表明，赫格斯和政府可能对这个国家的解读是错误的。

paras.en: Garen Wintemute, director of the Violence Prevention Research Program at the University of California, Berkeley, said survey data points to a declining appetite for violence in the US.
paras.zh: 加州大学伯克利分校暴力预防研究项目主任加伦·温特穆特表示，调查数据表明美国对暴力的兴趣正在下降。

paras.en: "This morning, the chair of the US Conference of Catholic Bishops labeled this [livestream execution announcement] as barbaric," he said. "And I think he speaks for a lot of people."
paras.zh: “今天早上，美国天主教主教会议主席称这种[直播处决公告]是野蛮的，”他说。 “我认为他代表了很多人。”

paras.en: "I think it's this: A public execution is not who we are," he added. "It's not who we aspire to be as a country."
paras.zh: “我认为这就是：公开处决不是我们的身份，”他补充道。 “这不是我们作为一个国家渴望成为的样子。”

paras.en: Vice-President JD Vance, a Catholic, has said he would not be watching the execution.
paras.zh: 副总统 JD 万斯是一位天主教徒，他表示他不会观看死刑执行过程。

paras.en: President Donald Trump dodged the question of whether he'd tune in himself - but confirmed he approved the decision to livestream Hasan's death.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统回避了他是否会亲自收听的问题，但确认他批准了直播哈桑之死的决定。

paras.en: "I really don't care how he goes as long as he goes," Trump said. "And I think that the death penalty is a very worthy way of going for him."
paras.zh: 特朗普说：“我真的不在乎他怎么样，只要他走就行。” “我认为死刑对他来说是一种非常值得的方式。”

articles.title: Cool chemistry trick allows new tattoos to 'turn on and off'
articles.author: Kenna Hughes-Castleberry

paras.en: Researchers have developed a new type of tattoo ink that can be switched on and off with light, allowing colors and images embedded in the skin to be changed and even "erased" without having to go through the painful tattoo-removal process.

The system, which is being commercialized under the name PhotoTat, could eventually give people a way to conceal or change permanent body art. It could also have more practical applications, including medical tattoos that are visible only when a doctor needs to see them, researchers reported in a study published Friday (Oct. 9) in the journal Matter & Light.

"This is a tattoo that you can have, and whenever you decide you don't want it to be showing anymore, or you just don't want it there, you just turn it off," said study co-author Carson Bruns, an associate professor of biomedical engineering at the University of Colorado at Boulder. "And that's it. You don't have to turn it on again."

PhotoTat contains three primary color inks — blue, magenta and yellow — made with photochromic dyes, which are light-sensitive compounds that can change color with different wavelengths of light. These dyes are encapsulated in nanoparticles of polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) — a medical-grade, glass-like plastic that is already used in medical implants and dermal fillers.

The dyes change their molecular structure when exposed to specific wavelengths of light. A 365-nanometer ultraviolet (UV) LED can activate pigments in around two to three seconds, Bruns said. Once activated, the colors can persist for hours to days under typical indoor lighting. But once the wearer exposes their skin to the bright outdoor sun, the colors disappear in seconds, erased by the intense light.

That makes the tattoo unique, as the pigment itself remains in the skin but the tattoo's appearance changes. Bruns and his team found that all three PhotoTat channels remained switchable in the skin for between 1.4 and 2.2 years.

The three colors enable someone to activate different portions of a tattoo using different wavelengths of light. That means the magenta part of the tattoo might be turned on with green light, while the yellow pigment would be activated by blue light. This allows the wearer to customize their design and coloration to whatever they want at the moment — from a purple cherry to a yellow group of hearts.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.
That feature makes PhotoTat appealing for "people who love tattoos and have lots of tattoos, but just want something kind of fun and playful to add," Bruns told Live Science.
Bruns has tested each iteration of PhotoTat's inks on his own skin. His art is arranged in a series of tattooed scales, with different ink formations in individual scales.

"I gave myself these scales on purpose because they're each sort of a container for an experiment," Bruns said. The result, he joked, resembles a "magical mermaid trick," with some scales appearing out of nowhere and others changing color when activated.
The technology can also be combined with conventional tattoo ink. A permanent black ink design, for example, could contain hidden PhotoTat elements that appear only when activated.

The new tattoos could be appealing to people who want tattoos but are hesitant about their permanence, as well as to people who love their tattoos but occasionally need to conceal them because of work, social expectations or family, Bruns said.
"It's going to be on for most of the time, but just for this one moment, I'm going to turn it off for you grandma, for example," Bruns said.

Bruns thinks the tattoos could be helpful in a medical setting, too. Patients undergoing radiation therapy, for example, sometimes receive permanent tattoos that help doctors precisely align radiation beams. While useful, those marks remain after the treatment, reminding the patient of their experience. These would make such markings invisible if a patient wants them to be.
PhotoTat could potentially allow similar markings to be switched on during surgery and hidden afterward.

Bruns has spent several years developing other smart tattoos for medical applications, including a dosimeter-type tattoo that measures the amount of UV radiation a wearer experiences, along with a tattoo that changes color when the wearer is exposed to dangerous gamma radiation.

"It's not for you and me, but if you're like an astronaut or a nuclear engineer, they have to wear these dosimeters," Bruns said. "So, we have like a dosimeter tattoo that sort of puts that in your skin."
So far, Bruns and a fellow tattoo artist, have only commercialized the purple PhotoTat ink, after running the ink through a series of third-party medical tests.

The tests showed the purple is safe for use, and available to order, but it isn't cheap at $100 for a small bottle. Bruns hopes as more research is done, he can bring the other colors to market and lower the production cost, so the technology is more accessible.

articles.title: Scientists have identified a 'protein signature' in blood that could predict healthy aging
articles.author: Zunnash Khan

paras.en: Two people born on the exact same day can age in totally different ways — one in relative health and the other with chronic disease. Now, scientists have found a key difference in the immune systems of people who are more prone to age-related conditions, and it could help explain why some people remain healthier longer.

In young people, the immune system contains many naive T cells, a type of white blood cell. Over time, exposure to pathogens and vaccinations transforms some of these T cells into memory cells, which can respond quickly to defend the body against germs.
These memory cells make different types of characteristic proteins, called granzymes, which kill infected cells. They come in different "flavors," including granzyme K and granzyme B.

In a new study, published Friday (Oct. 9) in the journal Immunity, scientists found that individuals with more memory cells that make granzyme K than cells that make granzyme B tend to have healthier aging.

In the future, the balance of cells making granzyme K and granzyme B in a person's blood could be used as a test to determine "whether you're on the right trajectory of aging or not," study co-author Maxim Artyomov, an immunologist at Washington University in St. Louis, told Live Science.
Hunting for a signature of healthy aging

In earlier research, the same team found that, in old lab mice, granzyme K-making cells accumulated in several tissues and were linked to inflammation. They also observed the same increase in granzyme K cells in blood samples from older adults.
In the new study, they uncovered another piece of the puzzle: a dynamic with granzyme B-producing cells.
Get the world’s most fascinating discoveries delivered straight to your inbox.

They began by analyzing immune cells sampled from over 2,600 people ages 18 to 97, looking at the balance of granzyme K- and granzyme B-making cells. They found that people with a lower ratio of granzyme K to granzyme B cell populations were more likely to have autoimmune diseases or other chronic immune conditions.

In a second analysis, they looked at both immune cells and blood-borne proteins sampled from 329 people, using the data to pinpoint a "protein signature" linked to an abundance of granzyme B-making cells.

They went on to hunt for this protein signature in around 48,000 participants who'd provided data to the UK Biobank, a large database of health data from U.K.-based adults. People who were predicted to have higher levels of granzyme B-making cells based on their blood proteins had worse health outcomes in the following 17 years, with a higher risk of death and of conditions like diabetes, high blood pressure, and liver and kidney disease.
The findings might point to an aspect of immune aging that wasn't previously understood.

"I think that's really exciting," Claire Gustafson, an immunologist at the Allen Institute, said of the results. "It highlights there's potentially some novel biology that we haven't really observed before," Gustafson, who was not involved in the research, told Live Science.

However, while there's a strong association between the balance of these cell populations and disease risks, Artyomov emphasized that the study does not prove that this ratio directly causes the poor health outcomes. Further studies would be needed to understand why having more granzyme B cells is linked with poorer health.
"This observation might be just a consequence, not a cause of the disease," Artyomov noted.

It's also important to note that granzyme K-making cells in mice are not the same as granzyme K-making cells in humans. In mice, they represent a more mature, specialized stage of immune cell development, whereas in humans, granzyme B cells better fit that description, he told Live Science.

That points to a key way that immunity in mice and humans is different, which was "underappreciated" before, Gustafson said. So when we're comparing these cells in mice and humans, "we're not looking at apples to apples," she said. Scientists now specifically "need to look more into humans, as it's not reflected in animal models."

In people, immune cells' features can also vary across diverse human populations, Gustafson added. We need more data across different populations to get a "true understanding of universal immune health," she said. The K-to-B ratio may be a "novel" clue that can help scientists understand healthy aging, but more data is needed to unpack why and how that ratio is linked to healthy or unhealthy aging.
"This is kind of like the first step to be able to get there," she told Live Science.

articles.title: Self-driving, solar-powered cars that talk to each other? What vehicles might look like in 10 years.
articles.author: Skyler Ware

paras.en: Imagine you're road-tripping across the country 10 years from now. You spend a few minutes charging your electric vehicle and then set off — and your car's solar paint keeps it charged as you drive.

Your eyes are on the stunning scenery, taking in the vistas along Route 66 or the grandeur of the Rocky Mountains, or you're catching up on messages. Your hands barely touch the wheel, and your foot doesn't push a pedal. Your car communicates with others on the road, so there's no need to brake suddenly or swerve. That's because it knows a vehicle five cars up from you has done so, and all those in between are slowing at exactly the right pace to avoid dramatic changes in trajectory.

And when you park for the night, your car makes you money, selling the excess energy it's harvested from its paint back to the grid. Or maybe you don't feel like being in the driver's seat at all, so you hail a self-driving car and take a nap in the back seat in between adventures.

Some of that scenario may become a reality in the next 10 years, at least for those who are using the most cutting-edge cars on the market. Although there's some heavy speculation involved in that futuristic vision, vehicle manufacturers are already incorporating increasingly sophisticated automated driving technology into high-end personal vehicles, and self-driving taxis are coming to dozens of U.S. cities.

What's more, dramatic changes in range, cost and charging speed for electric vehicles (EVs) are arriving at a rapid pace. While some of these technologies may not wind up in personal cars, others are already taking to the roads.

Some car models within the next decade may interact with their surroundings in new ways, including by communicating with other cars to avoid collisions, drawing energy from natural sources, or letting drivers get paid for sending their cars' unused energy back to the grid.

If you're driving an EV, you might avoid the hassle of finding a charger when you're at work or running errands. In 2024, EV company Aptera unveiled a prototype car equipped with solar panels. Those panels — on the car's hood, roof, dashboard and hatch — allow the vehicle to travel about 40 miles (64 kilometers) per day on solar power. That's more than the average American drives per day. Aptera's vehicle can also travel up to 400 miles (640 km) on a standard electrical charge.

Some sunlight-powered cars might ditch the solar panels altogether in favor of a more integrated design. In 2024, Mercedes-Benz revealed it was researching a photovoltaic paint that could convert sunlight into energy for electric cars. In sunny cities such as Los Angeles, the company calculated, the paint could draw in enough energy to power the car for nearly 7,500 miles (12,000 km) per year. The tiny particles in the paint convert about 20% of the energy from sunlight into electricity, which is comparable to the efficiency of existing solar panels.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: You might even be able to sell some of the energy stored in your car's battery back to the grid. EV owners could charge during the day or late at night, when the demand for electricity is lower and pay lower rates for electricity. Then, in the evenings when the electrical grid is under more strain and the price of electricity is higher, they could sell that stored energy back at a profit.

Standardized software programs that throttle EV charging speeds during peak hours already exist. Drivers can use them if, for example, they want to keep charging costs down by primarily charging their cars during off-peak hours when electricity costs are lower, or if they want to use electricity only from solar power to charge, said Rajit Gadh, a researcher who studies EV charging and scalability at UCLA. But the process for sending energy back to the grid is a different story. Individual manufacturers haven't yet landed on a standard way to tell cars when and how much energy to discharge, Gadh said.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: "What is needed is really [for] every EV charging vendor — and every EV manufacturer, actually — to have this protocol built in, adhere to it in its full specification, and make it available," Gadh told Live Science.

With the right protocols, though, cars of the future will be able to do more than interface with the electrical grid. "Vehicle-to-everything" technologies could enable cars to communicate with infrastructure and other vehicles to avoid traffic and collisions.

Some cars today are already equipped with vehicle-to-vehicle (V2V) communications. These systems use short-range radio signals to alert other V2V-equipped vehicles of the car's speed, direction of travel and braking patterns. The radio signals can travel about 1,000 feet (300 meters), allowing the vehicle to receive data from cars that are not in the driver's line of sight.

V2V systems could help reduce traffic collisions by warning drivers about oncoming cars they can't see yet — for example, by alerting a driver to another car speeding toward an intersection or coming around a bend as the driver is passing another vehicle on a twisty, two-lane highway. Not all cars have the technology, though, so its practical utility is limited for now.

Some driver assistance technologies, such as lane departure warnings and cruise control, have been on the market in personal cars for decades. These technologies and more recent assistive features require the driver to be in control of the vehicle, but theoretically, they make driving easier. For example, Tesla's Full Self-Driving (Supervised) mode handles most steering and braking tasks, but safe operation requires the driver to keep their eyes on the road and be ready to take over at a moment’s notice. In the next several years, drivers will likely see new features that automate driving in more contexts.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Some of these features will allow drivers to take their attention off the road entirely and enjoy some in-car entertainment, as long as they're alert and able to retake control of the vehicle within a few seconds if conditions change. Technologies that fully automate driving in many circumstances within certain service areas will likely be in about 4% of cars on the market by 2035, according to a white paper from the World Economic Forum.

In cars equipped with these features, "you're still going to have driver controls, but under certain circumstances, it will be effectively an automated vehicle," Luke Neurauter, who leads the Division of Vehicle, Driver and System Safety at the Virginia Tech Transportation Institute, told Live Science.

Mercedes-Benz introduced its Drive Pilot system for two consumer car lines in 2022. On the entire German Autobahn network and on certain freeways between and around Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas, during heavy traffic, the system lets the driver turn their attention toward other activities, such as reading a book or eating lunch, while the car handles steering and keeping pace with other nearby vehicles.

But as the artificial intelligence (AI) models that control autonomous driving improve and become better able to handle unusual scenarios — often called "edge" or "corner" cases — on the road, drivers will be able to hand over control to their cars in more situations, said Rahul Jain, an electrical and computer engineer at the University of Southern California.

Future AI systems might "have some reasoning ability, and then because of that, it can handle these corner cases much better than current systems are able to do," Jain told Live Science. For example, a car might be able to better respond to an indecisive pedestrian who suddenly enters a crossing, assess whether to enter potentially hazardous conditions such as flooded roads, or safely navigate around unusual circumstances, such as construction work, on a highway.

While some systems will enable drivers to make fewer decisions, others that may roll out in the next several years will track a driver's attention and alert them with sounds, an indicator light or haptic feedback when their focus falters. These systems use cameras and software to track head position, eye movement and steering-wheel input to ensure drivers are focused on the road even when they're using assistive features such as lane centering, Neurauter said.

In addition to looking for distracted driving, the technology might expand to monitor drivers for fatigue and alcohol impairment, he added. That information could then affect "whether or not other features become active, or change how they act, based on the driver state at that moment in time," Neurauter said. Proposed legislation could make this technology a requirement in new vehicles as early as 2027, but technological hurdles and concerns over privacy and false positives could stall its implementation.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The technology could also assist drivers who become unable to safely operate the vehicle — for example, if the driver falls asleep or experiences a medical emergency. If a car detects that the driver is not holding the steering wheel or actively controlling the vehicle, it could send a series of visible, audible, or tactile alerts. If the driver doesn’t respond to those cues, a car might turn on its hazard lights and come to a stop. Some vehicle manufacturers are already rolling out such technology; for example, Volkswagen has made it available in all new vehicles from model year 2025.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: While personal cars may not offer full automation, highly automated car services will become much more common as rideshare vehicles in major metro areas. In some cities, like San Francisco, commuters already rely heavily on autonomous vehicles from Waymo. The company has rolled out its cars in nearly a dozen cities — including Dallas, Houston, Atlanta and Los Angeles — and has announced plans to expand service to more than 20 additional locales. Other companies — such as Nuro and Volkswagen’s MOIA — are testing their vehicles with human drivers on board before rolling out full public service.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Currently, autonomous vehicles navigate by combining information from preloaded, high-resolution maps and real-time radar, lidar and visual data collected by cameras and sensors attached to the car. An onboard computer uses that information to build a 3D map of its surroundings. Right now, the cost of these sensors makes them impractical for consumer vehicles, Jain said, but they’re becoming cheaper as manufacturers scale up production. The cars also use an AI model trained on both common and unusual driving situations to anticipate how other vehicles and pedestrians will behave and plot a safe path forward, Jain added.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Developing those high-resolution maps takes time, which is one of the main reasons autonomous rideshares aren’t available everywhere yet. Mapping usually involves decking out a car with high-end visual sensors and lasers and driving it throughout the region. Although cities like San Francisco have been mapped with this level of precision, much of the U.S. has not.
"It's very difficult to do overnight," said John Dolan, an autonomous-driving researcher at the Carnegie Mellon University Robotics Institute.

Complexities also tend to arise in city environments, where unexpected stops are more common and there are many pedestrians who behave unpredictably or jaywalk. But interstate highway driving doesn't face as many of those obstacles, and that could enable autonomous long-haul drives.

"[Autonomous] trucking, I would expect, would be the first thing that's going to happen" in terms of autonomous travel outside of major cities, Jain said. A few driverless trucks are already on the road: Pittsburgh-based company Aurora deployed the technology on I-45 in Texas, between Dallas and Houston, in 2025, with plans to expand across the southern U.S.
While there's speculation involved in predicting the range of self-driving capabilities available in a decade, the picture for EVs is a little clearer.

Right now, lithium-ion batteries dominate the EV market. Each cell in a lithium-ion battery has two electrodes, commonly a layered graphite electrode and a metal oxide or phosphate electrode, separated by a liquid electrolyte solution. Lithium ions migrate back and forth between these two electrodes when a person charges and discharges the battery.

Many electric cars with lithium-ion batteries can already travel more than 300 miles (480 km) on a charge. But that's not ideal for a long-range car trip, because charging stations are few and far between in the country's vast interior and charging takes longer than filling up a gas tank.

Solid-state batteries, which replace the liquid electrolyte with a solid electrolyte made of ceramic, polymer or sulfide materials, could make that cross-country trip in an EV a practical option, allowing an electric car to travel more than 750 miles (1,200 km) on a single charge. Some prototype battery packs can already achieve this range under controlled conditions. If a solid electrolyte were paired with an anode made of pure lithium, rather than graphite or hard carbon, it would allow the battery to store more energy than a lithium-ion cell of similar mass can.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Solid-state batteries may also enable faster charging. In current batteries that use liquid electrolytes, charging and discharging the battery too quickly can cause dendrites, thin branches of lithium that stretch across the cell and short-circuit the battery. A solid electrolyte could, in theory, block those dendrites, which would enable cars to charge fully in just 10 to 15 minutes. The higher energy density from a lithium metal anode also translates to a greater range than that from a similarly sized lithium-ion battery, Eric Wachsman, director of the Maryland Energy Innovation Institute at the University of Maryland, told Live Science.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Many of the raw materials that go into existing lithium-ion batteries are concentrated in a handful of geographic areas. In 2023, Australia, China and Chile mined about 85% of that year's lithium supply; China mined the majority of graphite used that year as well. And battery materials still make up a significant portion of an electric vehicle's cost.

Sodium-ion batteries could be cheaper and easier to source. Sodium is plentiful in Earth's crust, which means mining could be done throughout the U.S., potentially with a comparatively low environmental impact.

Such batteries also rely on a more widely available electrode material. Sodium ions are larger than lithium ions, so they don't fit in between layers of graphite like lithium ions do. Instead, sodium-ion batteries use hard carbon electrodes.

"When you cook at home and your soup boils over and you get this black ring around your pot, this is hard carbon," Maximilian Fichtner, a solid-state chemist at the Helmholtz Institute Ulm for Electrochemical Energy Storage in Germany, told Live Science. "You can produce this from sucrose or from biomass, from whatever. You can do that everywhere."

The downside is that hard carbon holds less sodium than graphite holds lithium, said Eric McCalla, a battery materials chemist at McGill University in Canada. That means sodium-ion batteries can't store as much energy relative to their mass, and they don't last quite as long as their lithium counterparts.
"The range won't be as large," McCalla told Live Science. "It'll be a fantastic commuter car, but you're not going to go on a family trip from Montreal to California so easily."

Manufacturers are already bringing sodium-ion technology to market. For instance, the Chinese company CATL began mass-producing the batteries in February and claims that their battery packs enable EV ranges over 250 miles (400 km).

But new technologies are being developed rapidly. For example, some scientists are making sodium-ion batteries that use solid electrolytes, combining the higher energy density of solid-state lithium batteries with the cost savings of sodium batteries.

This hybrid battery chemistry is still in the early stages of development, experts told Live Science. "I would be surprised to see them in cars in the next decade," McCalla told Live Science in an email. "I've been surprised before, though."
The future we're describing is the utopian scenario. But the biggest obstacles are likely not technological but rather regulatory, economic, political or cultural, experts said.

"We're going to try to guess at a timeline of when some of these things are going to come in, and odds are, we're going to be wrong," McCalla told Live Science. "Odds are, we're going to be slower than we think."

Solar panels may not wind up being the most economic or practical way to increase EVs' range, while scaling up manufacturing capacity for next-generation batteries is expensive and could slow EV adoption in the U.S. The utility of vehicle-to-vehicle communications, meanwhile, could be limited by a slow rollout and adoption of V2V-equipped cars among drivers.

Whether EVs will be ubiquitous will likely come down to their affordability relative to gas-powered vehicles, which is affected not just by manufacturing and technological advances but also domestic policy choices, such as whether to subsidize EVs or their charging networks.

One challenge for manufacturers is that the automated features drivers prefer may not always be safer. A recent review of automated systems found that those focused on driver safety, such as automatic safety or lane centering, tend to reduce crashes, while those focused on comfort, such as adaptive cruise control, can increase accidents. The authors proposed that such systems make it easier for people to disengage or become distracted while driving and possibly overestimate the capabilities of the system.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: And there are other kinks to work out for autonomous rideshare vehicles. In December 2025, a horde of Waymos stalled during a power outage, clogging San Francisco intersections. The cars are programmed to treat dark traffic signals as four-way stops, according to a statement from Waymo, but they occasionally ping human operators for confirmation. During the outage, the number of confirmation requests spiked, leading to delayed responses — and lengthy traffic jams. The company says it has since released software updates that allow its vehicles to act more decisively at dark signals. But questions remain about how the fleet will respond in natural disasters, and some have expressed frustration that autonomous rideshare vehicles already slow down ambulances, fire trucks and police cars responding to emergencies.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: One of the biggest roadblocks to automated driving is the regulatory environment, Neurauter said. Regulations on self-driving vehicles vary by state, and some, such as New York, effectively prohibit driverless vehicles entirely. Where they are legal, they often must carry higher insurance and pass testing, which could limit their rollout.

"When we get into automated driving, the driving behavior is being governed by software that's installed on a computer that's in the vehicle," Steven Shladover, a research engineer at the University of California, Berkeley, told Live Science. "That gets us into a messy gray area where both the federal and the state roles kind of overlap, and that's politically very complicated." For example, different states could end up with different rules for establishing who's legally responsible for an accident involving automated driving.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: In 10 years, you'll almost certainly be able to drive from Los Angeles to Las Vegas in an autonomous vehicle. But if you want to drive to New York City, you might have to stop in New Jersey — and take a train into the city.

Her work has also appeared in Science News Explores, ZME Science and Chembites, among others. Skyler has a Ph.D. in chemistry from Caltech.
